title.rendered: How to get the Dollie skin in Fortnite | Lost Dolls bundle items list

content.rendered:
Fortnite has been consistently shipping spooky cosmetics into the Item Shop, in line with the Halloween-themed Fortnitemares event, and Dollie is one of the original skins created for this very occasion. In the Lost Dolls category, besides Dollie, there are Mineko and Peppa Pinns as well.

Unlike a chunk of the skins released recently, these cosmetics aren’t the result of any third-party collab but are original designs created by Fortnite devs. Additionally, this is their first stint in the online multiplayer title, having only debuted on October 9.

While the aforementioned three skins can be purchased individually for 1,200 V-Bucks each, you can alternatively grab the Lost Dolls Bundle, which comes with extras, for 2,300 V-Bucks. Moreover, these items are only available in the Shop until October 15, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

Steps to claim the Dollie skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the Fortnitemares section and select it.
  3. Then, scroll down to the Locker of Horrors category and select your desired skin.
  4. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

All Lost Dolls bundle items in Fortnite

The following cosmetics are all the items that are included in the Lost Dolls Bundle. Their individual prices and respective bundled freebies are also listed below.

1. Dollie

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Doll Eyes wrap

2. Mineko

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Glowing Blossom wrap

3. Pippa Pinns

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Baneful Blaster wrap

4. Dollie’s Dark Portrait back bling

Price: 300 V-Bucks

5. Baneful Bunbun back bling

Price: 400 V-Bucks

6. Sakura Shamisen pickaxe and back bling

Price: 800 V-Bucks

7. Music Box Mannequin emote

Price: 400 V-Bucks

8. Glowing Blossom wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

9. Doll Eyes wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

10. Baneful Blaster wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

Wrapping up

Fortnitemares 2026 has turned out to be a rather remarkable rendition this time, at least in terms of cosmetics content. From original skins such as Dollie to major third-party collab skins such as Sora (Kingdom Hearts) and Joker (Persona), cosmetic items have come out at a consistent cadence and also feature an intriguing amount of variety among them.

Over the final few weeks of Fortnitemares and Fortnite Override itself, both of which will run till October 31, a few more popular collabs are set to make their way into the Item Shop. This forthcoming lineup features names such as Hazbin Hotel, Obsession, and The Purge. It will be interesting to see how the players, a sizable section of whom have been excitedly awaiting a few of these IPs, receive the content drop once it’s out.

title.rendered: Fortnite x Yeat crossover: Release time, items, and price

content.rendered:
Yeat is joining Fortnite’s Icon Series, and his bundle hits the Item Shop on October 15, 2026, at 8:00 PM ET (5:00 PM PT). It’s the rapper’s first full set of outfits in the game; until now he only had two Icon emotes, GEEK TIMË and COMË N GO.

Epic confirmed the collab on October 14 with the “Real Lyfe” trailer, which shows two Yeat outfits set to “If We Being Real.” The drop lines up with the v42.40 update, the last major patch of Chapter 7 Season 4, and lands in the middle of Fortnitemares 2026.

When does the Fortnite x Yeat collab release?

The Item Shop resets at 00:00 UTC, so anyone east of the Americas gets Yeat on October 16.

Everything in the Fortnite x Yeat icon series bundle

Epic hasn’t published an item list. Leaker ShiinaBR and esports.gg report the set below; the trailer backs up the outfits, wrap and kicks.

  • 2 Outfits: one with an Alternate Style, one with a Reactive Style
  • 2 Back Blings
  • 1 Pickaxe
  • 2 Emotes
  • 1 Microphone (Festival instrument)
  • 1 Wrap
  • 1 Kicks

Three Jam Tracks are coming, but only one sits in the bundle

Yeat brings three songs to Fortnite Festival: If We Being Real, Money So Big and Get Busy. According to Beebom, one is packed into the bundle and the other two sell separately in the Item Shop.

If Jam Tracks follow their usual pricing, each standalone track will cost 500 V-Bucks.

Epic hasn’t confirmed the price yet

No price has been announced. Based on recent Icon sets, expect each outfit at around 1,500 V-Bucks and the full bundle at roughly 3,000–3,500 V-Bucks.

The closest comparison is Madison Beer’s bundle from September. It had two outfits, a mic, emotes and Jam Tracks, and it sold for 3,400 V-Bucks (our Madison Beer guide lists every item price).

We’ll update this post with exact prices once the shop goes live.

There’s no free way to get Yeat right now

Some Icon sets launch with an Icon Cup that awards the outfit early, as Madison Beer’s did. Epic hasn’t announced one for Yeat, so the Item Shop is the only confirmed route. For other options, see our free Fortnite skins guide.

Wrapping up

Yeat lands as Chapter 7 Season 4 winds down, alongside v42.40’s new Honey and Obsession Sprites. Epic hasn’t said how long the bundle will stay in the shop; Madison Beer’s set stayed for about ten days, so don’t wait too long.

Festival Season 15 is still headlined by Lil Tecca, so Yeat isn’t this season’s Festival Icon. Watch the Season 16 reveal for the next music collab.

Are you picking up the Yeat bundle, or just the Jam Tracks? Let us know in the comments.

FAQs

Is Yeat the Fortnite Festival Season 15 Icon?

No. Lil Tecca is the Season 15 Festival Icon. Yeat joins through the Icon Series in the Item Shop.

Can you get the Yeat skin for free?

Not at the moment. Epic hasn’t announced a Yeat Icon Cup, so you’ll need V-Bucks.

Which update adds Yeat?

Yeat arrives alongside v42.40, which also adds the Honey and Obsession Sprites, six Loot Hacks and new Match Overrides.

Will the Yeat bundle return to the Item Shop?

Icon sets usually return, but Epic hasn’t shared a return date.

acceptedAnswer.text: There could be several reasons. However, you can easily troubleshoot the Always On display when it’s not working on your Apple Watch to get it working again.

mainEntity.name: Why does the display dim when Always On is enabled?

acceptedAnswer.text: The display dims in Always On mode to conserve battery life. Keeping the screen at full brightness constantly would drain the battery much faster. Therefore, Apple has designed the Always On feature to tone down the brightness when your Apple Watch is idle.

mainEntity.name: Do all watch faces support Always On?

acceptedAnswer.text: As mentioned earlier, the Always On feature simplifies the visuals of the watch face and displays essential information when it is idle. Therefore, in Always On mode, the watch face may not appear as it normally does.

mainEntity.name: Does Optimized Battery Charging slow down charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your iPhone charges at normal speed up to 80%. The last 20% is intentionally delayed to protect battery health, but you can override this if needed.

mainEntity.name: Does it work with fast charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fast charging is supported up to 80%. The optimization only affects the timing of the final portion of the charge.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to leave on all the time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. For most users, keeping the feature enabled is the best way to preserve battery health. If your needs change, you can always disable it.

mainEntity.name: What if my routine is unpredictable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The feature works best with consistent charging habits. If your schedule varies, you may not see the full benefits, but it won't harm your device.

title.rendered: Anime Zero: All accessories and how to unlock them

content.rendered:
Accessories are a crucial aspect of Anime Zero, as they allow you to amp up your weapon’s strength and take on tougher dungeons packed with enemies. However, crafting them can cost valuable resources, so it’s crucial to know which stat boosts each accessory brings to the table before committing to one. Not only that, but knowing your options also helps you decide whether there’s a better alternative worth investing in.

On top of that, the latest Update 3 (Void Arbiter) added 13 new accessories, bringing the total to 27. So, to make things easier, here’s a complete list of all the accessories in Anime Zero and how you can unlock each of them easily!

Complete list of accessories in Anime Zero

Keep in mind that each Anime Zero accessory requires different crafting materials. They all offer unique stat boosts, such as weapon damage, HP, EXP, drop rates, and others. With that out of the way, here’s a complete list of all the accessories in the game, with the ones added in Update 3 marked as (New)

Also check out: Anime Zero codes

How to unlock accessories in Anime Zero

Of course, the next big question is: how do you unlock accessories in Anime Zero? To do so, you’ll need to craft them using specific resources. Simply go out and collect all of the materials required for the accessory you want to obtain, as we’ve mentioned above. You can farm them in Story and Infinite Mode runs, or buy some of them from the Shop tab in the crafting menu.

Once you have everything, open the Areas option and choose Crafting from the menu. Then, head to Yugi the Forger, select the accessory from the Craft tab, and hit Quick Craft.

Keep in mind that you can equip up to four accessories at once, one each in the head, face, neck, and back slots. So, instead of crafting accessories at random, pick the best option for each slot.

Wrapping up

There are 27 accessories in Anime Zero, and each of them offers different stat boosts to improve your weapons. Crafting these accessories is important for progressing through the game, as they can help you steamroll dungeons and defeat enemies.

title.rendered: Universal Monsters skins return to Fortnite after nearly four years

content.rendered:
The Mummy, Frankenstein’s Monster, and Frankenstein’s Bride from the Universal Monsters franchise are back in Fortnite. The three skins first arrived in October 2021 and were last sold in the Item Shop in November 2022. That makes this return their first in nearly four years, timed for the ongoing Halloween event, Fortnitemares 2026.

Each skin costs 1,200 V-Bucks. The Mummy and Frankenstein’s Monster each come with a free back bling, while Frankenstein’s Bride is sold on her own. The Mummy is also part of the Mummy Bundle for 1,600 V-Bucks.

At the time of writing, the Universal Monsters cosmetics are listed in the Item Shop until October 16, 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET. If you’ve waited years for one of these classic monsters, use the steps below before they rotate out.

Steps to get the Universal Monsters skins in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Universal Monsters section and select the skin you want.
  3. On the next screen, press and hold the Purchase button to complete the transaction.

If you want The Mummy along with his pickaxe and wrap, the Mummy Bundle is the better pick. It includes The Mummy, Smallcophagus, Ancient Staff, and Mummified for 1,600 V-Bucks.

All Universal Monsters cosmetics in Fortnite

1. The Mummy (outfit)

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Comes with: Smallcophagus back bling
Also available in: Mummy Bundle

Frankenstein’s Monster (outfit)

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Comes with: Monster Mind back bling

Frankenstein’s Bride (outfit)

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks

Ancient Staff (pickaxe)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Mummy Bundle

Grave Robber (pickaxe)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

Smallcophagus (back bling)

Comes with: The Mummy skin
Also available in: Mummy Bundle

Monster Mind (back bling)

Comes with: Frankenstein’s Monster skin

Mummified (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Mummy Bundle

Stitched Up (wrap)

Price: 300 V-Bucks

Wrapping up

Throughout Fortnite Override, recognizable IPs have brought both cosmetics and gameplay content into the game. For Halloween, that run has turned to horror. Five Nights at Freddy’s opened Fortnitemares on October 1, followed by Freddy Krueger and 99 Nights in the Forest.

With Chapter 7 Season 4 expected to wrap up around October 31, Epic has roughly two weeks left for more Halloween drops. Fortnitemares is in full swing, so more horror franchises could still join Fortnite’s long list of collabs before the month ends.

Can I get a Universal Monsters skin in Fortnite for free?

No. The Universal Monsters skins are sold only in the Item Shop for V-Bucks. There is no quest or event reward that unlocks them. If you’re short on V-Bucks, see our guide on ways to get free Fortnite skins.

Can I get all three Universal Monsters skins in one bundle?

No. In this rotation, only The Mummy has a bundle, the 1,600 V-Bucks Mummy Bundle. Frankenstein’s Monster and Frankenstein’s Bride are sold individually.

When did the Universal Monsters skins first come to Fortnite?

All three debuted during Fortnitemares 2021. Frankenstein’s Monster arrived first in early October, followed by The Mummy and then Frankenstein’s Bride later that month.

Which other horror collabs are in the Fortnite Item Shop right now?

As of this week’s shop, you can also buy cosmetics from Five Nights at Freddy’s, A Nightmare on Elm Street (Freddy Krueger), Stranger Things, and 99 Nights in the Forest.

title.rendered: iPhone Duo repair fees: $999 for the inner display, $1,499 for other damage

content.rendered:
Apple listed out-of-warranty repair fees for the iPhone Duo on October 14, according to MacRumors. Without AppleCare+, replacing the inner display costs $999, and the highest fee for other accidental damage is $1,499. With AppleCare+, both of those repairs cost $99.

Without AppleCare+, the inner display repair costs $999

The Duo’s two displays are priced as separate repairs, and the inner one is the most expensive screen fix on the list. The fees below are the ones MacRumors reported from that listing. They are U.S. prices, with the AppleCare+ fee in the last column.

The listing calls $1,499 the maximum for other damage, so it marks the top of that range. At $999, the inner display repair alone is half the Duo’s $1,999 starting price. The cover layer is the only repair under $100 without the plan, at $49. Battery service costs $229 without the plan. With AppleCare+, the battery is replaced at no charge when capacity drops below 80 percent.

One inner display repair makes the AppleCare+ plan cheaper

AppleCare+ with Theft and Loss for iPhone Duo costs $19.99 a month, $199.99 a year, or $399 upfront. Apple says the plan covers accidents like drops and spills, battery replacement, and theft and loss on eligible products, with priority support from Apple Experts.

With the plan, one inner display repair costs $498 in total: the $399 upfront price and the $99 fee. Without it, the same repair costs $999. That makes one inner display repair enough for the upfront plan to come out cheaper. The plan prices do not say how long the coverage lasts, so the $498 figure assumes one repair within the plan’s term. A theft or loss claim carries a $149 fee.

AppleCare One is a separate monthly plan that covers more than one device.

Duo fees run about double the iPhone 17 Pro’s without a plan

Apple’s 2025 fee list for the iPhone 17 Pro put other damage at $749 and the front screen at $329, both without AppleCare+. The Duo’s $1,499 for other damage is about double that. Its $999 inner display is about three times the iPhone 17 Pro front screen fee.

Both phones pay $99 with AppleCare+ for other accidental damage, so the difference for that repair sits entirely in the no-plan column.

Some repairs have no plan price, and the fees are estimates

The reported list has no AppleCare+ fee for rear camera damage, which costs $229 without the plan. It also has no plan fee for outer display and back glass damage together, which costs $509 without it. MacRumors reports that Apple calls the figures estimated repair fees, so check the current prices on Apple’s repair page before you decide.

Pre-orders open October 16, and the phone goes on sale October 23

The Duo starts at $1,999 in the US, or $83.29 a month for 24 months through Apple Card Monthly Installments. Pre-orders begin at 5 a.m. PT on October 16, general availability starts October 23, and 28 other countries and regions get it on October 30.

title.rendered: WhatsApp guest calling lets people without an account join a call

content.rendered:
WhatsApp announced guest calling on October 14. A WhatsApp user can now send a call link to someone who doesn’t have WhatsApp. That person joins from a computer browser after the host lets them in. WhatsApp’s examples are colleagues, classmates, and tutors, and the post says hosts don’t have to worry about which apps those people use.

Guests need only a link and a browser

Only people with a WhatsApp account can create a call link, so the host must have one. The host does three things:

  1. Opens the Calls tab and taps the + icon.
  2. Creates a call link and sends it.
  3. Admits the guest from the waiting room.

Guests type a name and wait until the host lets them in. The host can remove a guest at any time. The call-link panel in WhatsApp’s announcement artwork warns that anyone with the link can use it, so share it only with people you trust.

Apple’s FaceTime follows a similar pattern for Android and Windows users. The Apple user creates the link, and the guest joins in Chrome or Edge without being able to start a call. The setup is in how to use FaceTime on Android or PC.

Guests can share their screen but can’t invite others

Guests can share their computer screen to review materials, react with a thumbs up or heart, and raise a hand. They can’t see other participants’ phone numbers or send messages. They also can’t add anyone to the call directly.

Calls have no time limit and a 32-person cap

WhatsApp describes guest calls as free, end-to-end encrypted, and without time limits. That means no abrupt cutoffs, so nobody has to restart the call or wait for everyone to rejoin. One-to-one and group calls can include up to 32 people once the host admits them. A study group or a small team fits under that cap. Regular WhatsApp group calls also top out at 32 people, and how to make audio and video WhatsApp calls on iPhone, Mac, and web covers the group steps.

Zoom’s free Basic plan allows 100 people per meeting but caps each meeting at 40 minutes, according to Zoom’s pricing page. For a long call with up to 32 people, WhatsApp removes that limit. For 33 to 100 people, WhatsApp can’t hold the call, and Zoom’s free plan can.

Some coverage frames the launch as a challenge to Zoom and Google Meet. WhatsApp’s post names neither service, so this article compares only Zoom.

Calendar links are due later this year

WhatsApp plans calendar integrations for Google Calendar and Outlook later this year. Users will install a WhatsApp plugin, connect their account, and add a call link to an invite. Invitees can join with or without a WhatsApp account. Until those integrations launch, the call link has to go into the invite by hand. iPhone users can already schedule a WhatsApp call from the iPhone Calendar app.

Countries and phone access are still unclear

WhatsApp’s post doesn’t name the countries where guest calling is available. It also doesn’t say whether every account has the option yet. It describes guests joining from a computer browser and doesn’t say how a guest on a phone would join.

title.rendered: OpenAI reportedly agrees not to use Apple’s alleged trade secrets while the case runs

content.rendered:
According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has agreed not to use the trade secrets Apple accuses it of misusing, for as long as the lawsuit is pending. The commitment came at a hearing on Wednesday, October 14, before U.S. District Judge Edward Davila in San Jose. OpenAI denies the allegations, and the court has not ruled on whether they are true.

Apple sued OpenAI in July, naming OpenAI, io Products, and former Apple employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu. The case is Apple Inc. v. Liu in the Northern District of California. Apple alleges that the former employees used its proprietary information to help OpenAI develop hardware, and that they told new OpenAI hires how to avoid scrutiny when leaving Apple.

OpenAI agreed not to use the alleged secrets during the case

Bloomberg describes the commitment as voluntary, and says the judge can enforce it. The reporting does not say whether OpenAI filed it as a stipulation or whether it was entered as an order. The October 13 order does not mention the agreement. No statement from Apple or OpenAI on the agreement was available when this was written.

OpenAI will collect forensic images from 14 employees’ devices

OpenAI also agreed to collect forensic images from the devices of 14 employees that may hold Apple’s confidential information, Bloomberg reported. A forensic image is a full copy of a device’s data that investigators can examine later.

The judge had already flagged the risk of lost evidence. In the October 13 order, he called Apple’s argument that forensic data could be lost or overwritten "well-taken." He pointed to a conversation in which Liu and Alyssa Peng discussed restoring Apple-owned devices.

Apple gets early access to messages and interviews, not R&D files

Under the October 13 order, Apple can get three categories of material before the normal discovery schedule:

  • Forensic images the defendants have already collected
  • Documents used to interview Apple candidates for OpenAI’s hardware group, including scripts and summaries of interviews with Apple employees
  • LINE conversations between Liu and Peng since January 1, 2026

Apple’s request for OpenAI’s research files on metal finishes, power management, and battery functionality was denied. Those files will come through regular discovery. Liu, Tang Tan, and Peng must sit for depositions, and OpenAI and io Products must produce corporate witnesses.

The judge also deferred ruling on requests that use the term "Apple Originated Information." He called it "amorphous as currently defined" and gave Apple five days to propose a tighter version.

The judge is reportedly likely to back Apple on the injunction

Apple has asked for a preliminary injunction that would bar OpenAI from using any confidential information it acquired from Apple while the case goes on. At the hearing, Davila said he was "highly likely" to side with Apple, according to Bloomberg. No ruling has been reported yet.

OpenAI’s motion to dismiss argues that Apple has not identified any specific stolen trade secrets. OpenAI has said it has no need or desire for Apple’s trade secrets.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in July that the case could make it harder for OpenAI to keep its reported 2027 timeline for its first device. An injunction would limit how that hardware work can use Apple’s information.

The first deadline falls around October 18

Defendants must respond to the expedited requests within 14 days of the order, or within five days for materials they have already collected. The forensic images are in the five-day group, so they are due around October 18. The depositions follow within 30 days after Apple receives those responses.

The reporting gives no date for the injunction ruling.

mainEntity.name: Why isn’t the Always On display working on my Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: There could be several reasons. However, you can easily troubleshoot the Always On display when it’s not working on your Apple Watch to get it working again.

mainEntity.name: Why does the display dim when Always On is enabled?

title.rendered: Apple Intelligence is reportedly coming to China in December without Siri AI

content.rendered:
Apple plans to bring Apple Intelligence to mainland China in December, according to a Bloomberg report published October 14. The first launch would arrive in an iOS 27.3 update and leave out Siri AI, the assistant Apple announced this year. Apple has not confirmed the date or the update number.

Apple Intelligence has not been available in mainland China since it launched in 2024.

The launch would leave out Siri AI and image generation

The report says the first set would include Genmoji, AI notification summaries, Writing Tools, and the Clean Up tool in Photos. Text generation would be limited in some apps. Image Playground and the newer version of Genmoji would be left out, along with Siri AI.

Apple’s October Apple TV 4K announcement says Siri AI is still in beta and launches in English in eight countries and regions. It is not initially available in the EU on iOS or iPadOS.

These are mostly features Apple first introduced in 2024. References in macOS 26.7 code had already pointed to Writing Tools coming to China with content restrictions, but that was code, not an announcement.

Alibaba supplies the models, with a government filter

Alibaba confirmed in July that its Qwen model will power Apple Intelligence features for Chinese users. It gave no timeframe. The report names Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang as the models, and says the setup includes guardrails, including a filter that lets the government approve ongoing model updates.

Reuters reported in August, citing three anonymous sources, that Apple trained a China-specific AI model with Alibaba’s help.

TechCrunch reported in July that a Baidu spokesperson confirmed the work, but a Reuters-based report says Baidu made no on-record statement. Bloomberg says the work covers search and Siri-related features.

China’s regulator listed Apple’s service in July

On July 15, the Cyberspace Administration of China published a notice listing seven phone on-device generative AI services with completed filings. Apple’s service appears on the list as “Apple智能.” Media called it approval, but the notice is a filing record and gives no launch date.

Permit records for newer iPhones, including the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, reportedly list the Alibaba models.

Apple has not confirmed a date yet

Apple made no announcement in late March, when Apple Intelligence briefly appeared for some iPhone users in mainland China before the update was pulled. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said the rollout was accidental.

Apple has still not announced a China date or commented publicly on the report. Its Apple Intelligence availability page says new Apple Intelligence features will not be available in China while Apple works through regulatory requirements.

The same page says that once Apple Intelligence reaches mainland China, devices bought earlier that support it will be able to switch on a core set of features there. Until Apple names a date, December rests on sources. The reports also do not explain why Siri AI is left out.

excerpt.rendered: Bloomberg reports Apple Intelligence could reach mainland China in December in iOS 27.3, without Siri AI. Alibaba would supply models, and Apple has not announced a date.

title.rendered: HomePod mini 2: Is it worth $149 before Siri AI arrives?

content.rendered:
Apple announced the HomePod mini 2 on October 13, 2026. Pre-orders opened the same day, and the speaker goes on sale in stores on October 30. It costs $149, which is $50 more than the original mini cost when it launched in 2020.

You get a new S10 chip, Thread support, and a light display on top right away. The feature Apple leads with, Siri AI, comes later as a free software update. So the real question is whether the speaker is worth $149 without it.

HomePod mini 2 specs at a glance

Apple’s spec page lists these. Thread matters most if you’re building a smart home, and Wi-Fi 6E only helps if your router supports the 6 GHz band.

HomePod mini 2 vs. Original HomePod mini: What’s new

The original mini shipped with an S5 chip. The S10 is the biggest hardware change, and Apple pairs it with computational audio that analyzes music in real time to adjust dynamic range, loudness, and acoustic performance.

Other changes:

  • Light display: Sound Glow sits on top of the speaker (more on that below).
  • Colors: Pink and green are new. Yellow and orange from the older lineup aren’t on the new list. Red, which Gurman reported Apple had tested, didn’t make it.
  • Sensors: Temperature and humidity sensing is now on Apple’s spec sheet.

How does HomePod mini 2 sound? (and what sound glow does)

Apple gives the speaker a full-range driver, dual passive radiators, and 360-degree sound. It doesn’t publish driver size or power output, so you can’t compare the audio on paper. If sound quality is the main reason to buy, check reviews first.

Sound Glow is the light show on top. It pulses in sync with the music, takes its colors from album art, and can run soundscape animations like rain. It’s fun, but it doesn’t change how the speaker sounds.

Is HomePod mini 2 worth $149?

The original mini was $129 after Apple’s June 2026 price increase, so the new one costs $20 more than that. The full-size HomePod costs $349, so the mini is still the cheaper way into Apple’s speaker lineup.

If you only want a speaker for music and timers, $20 for a faster chip and a light show is hard to justify on specs alone. The math gets better if you want the four-speaker Apple TV setup, which needs a mini 2 or a 2nd-generation HomePod.

When will HomePod mini 2 get Siri AI?

Siri AI debuted with iOS 27. Apple says it comes to the HomePod mini 2 as a free software update in the future, and it hasn’t given a date.

According to Apple, it adds:

  • Personal context, when paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad
  • Voice recognition for up to six people in the house
  • Broader world knowledge from the web
  • Better music discovery and more natural conversation

The limits matter more than the feature list:

  • The owner of the home needs an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad on the latest software, with Siri AI turned on.
  • It starts in English in the US, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the UK.
  • It won’t initially be available in the EU on iOS or iPadOS.
  • Some server-side features have daily limits, and Apple says expanded access will cost money later.

Apple hasn’t said whether the original mini gets Siri AI, so don’t assume it will. Apple says Siri requests can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, and that data processed in Private Cloud Compute isn’t stored or made accessible to Apple or anyone else.

HomePod mini 2 as a smart home hub

The mini 2 works as a home hub for HomeKit and Matter accessories. Once it’s set up with your iPhone or iPad, you can control them from the Home app when you’re away. The accessories themselves are sold separately.

Two things need a caveat:

  • Sound Recognition: It listens for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and sends alerts to your iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. It needs the updated Home setup and the latest software on every device. Apple says not to rely on it in an emergency, so keep your real alarms in place.
  • Sensors: The temperature and humidity sensors read best between 15°C and 30°C, at 30% to 70% humidity. The speaker needs time to settle after it starts up.

Also Read: Apple HomeView vs HomePod mini 2: What’s the difference, and which one should you buy?

How four-speaker surround sound works with Apple TV 4K

The new Apple TV 4K (4th generation) is the first Apple TV 4K to support four-speaker surround sound. You need four speakers in matching front and rear pairs, using HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation). Apple’s setup photo pairs two mini 2s with two full-size HomePods around the TV. The speakers detect where they sit in the room and set timing and levels on their own.

The Apple TV 4K costs $299 and ships November 13, so the setup can’t start before then. If you own one mini, you’d need three more speakers to use it this way.

Stereo pairs, Mac audio, and multiroom AirPlay

Two mini 2s make a stereo pair, but both must be the same model and generation. It also works as a speaker for a Mac with Wi-Fi 6E or later, and it can join multiroom AirPlay with other HomePods or AirPlay speakers.

Should you buy HomePod mini 2 or wait?

  • Buy it if you want a smart home hub that supports Thread and Matter, or you plan to build the four-speaker Apple TV setup.
  • Wait if Siri AI is the main reason. Apple hasn’t given a date, and it hasn’t said whether the original mini will get it.

Final thoughts

HomePod mini 2 is a real upgrade, even before Siri AI arrives. The S10 chip, Thread support, and Wi-Fi 6E make it a better smart home hub than the original. It’s also the cheapest way into Apple’s new four-speaker surround setup with Apple TV 4K. Sound Glow adds some personality, but it doesn’t change how the speaker sounds.

The problem is timing. Apple’s marketing leads with Siri AI, and that feature has no release date. Apple also hasn’t said whether the original mini will get it. That leaves you paying $149 today for hardware upgrades plus a promise.

If you’re building out a Matter or Thread smart home, or you’re planning the Apple TV surround setup after November 13, buy it now. If you mainly want a smarter Siri, your current mini will keep working fine until Apple gives a date. Wait for reviews and the software update before you spend.

  • Apple HomeView vs HomePod mini 2: What’s the difference?
  • HomePod mini 2 vs Echo Studio: Which speaker should you buy?

title.rendered: Apple HomeView vs HomePod mini 2: What’s the difference, and which one should you buy?

content.rendered:
Apple’s latest smart home devices take two very different approaches to making a home smarter. Apple HomeView puts a touchscreen, FaceTime camera, entertainment, and smart home controls in one place. Meanwhile, HomePod mini 2 focuses on music, Siri, and controlling connected devices through voice commands.

But is HomeView worth paying twice as much as HomePod mini 2? In this comparison, I’ll look at their key features, sound quality, smart home capabilities, pricing, and differences to help you decide which Apple device is right for your home.

Apple HomeView vs HomePod mini 2: What’s the difference?

Here’s how the two new home devices compare.

Apple HomeView vs HomePod mini 2: Design and display

The biggest difference becomes obvious when you imagine where each device would sit in your home.

HomeView features a 7-inch Liquid Retina touchscreen with a 1088 × 1088 resolution, True Tone, and a brightness range of 0.3 to 500 nits. The adjustable hinge makes it suitable for a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table. You can also choose a wall-mounted version for an entryway or hallway.

HomePod mini 2 takes up much less space. It measures 3.3 inches tall and 3.9 inches wide, weighs 0.74 pounds, and has a compact, spherical design covered in acoustic mesh fabric. Its illuminated touch surface handles playback, volume, and Siri controls.

My take: HomeView makes more sense in a shared family space where people regularly check information or adjust smart home settings. HomePod mini 2 can be considered for your desk, bookshelf, bedroom, or kitchen if you don’t need any visual features and want to save counter space.

Sound quality: Which device is better for music?

If music is the main reason you’re buying either device, I wouldn’t automatically assume HomeView is better just because it costs more.

HomePod mini 2 features a full-range driver, dual force-cancelling passive radiators, and a custom acoustic waveguide designed to produce 360-degree sound. Its S10 chip powers computational audio, which adjusts dynamic range, loudness, and acoustic performance in real time.

It also supports stereo pairing, multiroom audio through AirPlay, and a new Sound Glow feature. Sound Glow makes the illuminated top respond to music, creating a color-matched lighting effect based on the current song’s artwork.

HomeView has a more elaborate audio system in its tabletop version, combining two full-range drivers, a down-firing woofer, and dual force-cancelling passive radiators. It supports Spatial Audio and computational audio. The wall-mounted model uses two full-range drivers instead.

Which sounds better? HomeView has a larger acoustic system on paper, particularly in its tabletop model, while HomePod mini 2 delivers 360-degree audio from a compact body.

My take: If you want a compact speaker for everyday music, HomePod mini 2 is better. But to enjoy music alongside album artwork, lyrics, and other visual content, HomeView has the advantage.

Smart home controls: HomeView vs HomePod mini 2

This is where HomeView’s touchscreen can make a meaningful difference.

HomeView provides a visual dashboard for compatible smart lights, locks, thermostats, blinds, and cameras. You can tap the screen to adjust home accessories, check camera feeds, or activate scenes. Its Home Camera interface can display up to nine video feeds simultaneously.

HomePod mini 2 offers many of the same underlying smart home capabilities through Siri and Apple’s Home app. You can ask Siri to switch off lights, lock a compatible door, adjust the thermostat, or run a bedtime automation. It also works as a home hub, allowing you to control compatible accessories remotely through the Home app.

My take: I’d choose HomeView if I regularly monitor cameras or prefer tapping controls. I would go for HomePod mini 2 if I were only using voice commands to control lights, thermostats, and other connected devices.

Siri and Apple Intelligence: What changes?

Both devices are part of Apple’s move toward a more capable Siri, but there’s an important difference in availability.

HomeView includes the latest Siri AI. Apple says it offers broader world knowledge, more conversational responses, onscreen awareness, and personal context when paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. HomeView can also recognize up to six people and personalize supported content for each household member.

HomePod mini 2 has been announced with Siri AI as well, but the updated Siri experience will arrive in a future software update. That means you shouldn’t assume every new AI feature will be available on the speaker immediately.

Once enabled, Siri AI is designed to help HomePod mini 2 users have more natural conversations, discover music, and complete tasks using personal context from compatible Apple devices. Apple also says it can recognize up to six household members by voice.

My take: If you want Apple’s new Siri AI on your home hub immediately, HomeView has the advantage at launch. If you prefer a compact speaker and don’t mind waiting for the software update, HomePod mini 2 remains an interesting option.

Entertainment and everyday use

HomeView is designed to handle more than music playback. Its screen and camera make it useful for several everyday activities:

  • Video calls: Make FaceTime calls using Center Stage to keep participants framed.
  • Music and podcasts: Browse supported content and view animated album artwork and lyrics.
  • Cooking: Follow recipes, manage ingredients, and use hands-free timers.
  • Communication: Access supported Messages and Calendar features, and use Intercom to reach other rooms.
  • Home monitoring: Check compatible camera feeds and view useful smart home information.
  • Photos: Display personal memories and shared albums.

HomePod mini 2 keeps entertainment focused on audio. You can listen to music, podcasts, and news briefings, transfer audio using AirPlay, and use Siri to control playback. It can also serve as a speaker for compatible Macs.

What I found interesting is home theater support. When paired with the new Apple TV 4K, four HomePod mini 2 speakers can create a surround sound setup, with two speakers at the front and two at the rear. So, you can have a more immersive TV experience.

My take: As I often use my iPhone to follow recipes or make video calls around the house, HomeView seems more practical. If you mainly want background music while working, cooking, or relaxing, HomePod mini 2 can handle that without another screen.

Privacy and security: Which should you trust?

HomeView includes a camera, microphone, and display that can show personal information, so privacy deserves careful consideration.

Apple says HomeView recognizes household members by their faces and provides personalized experiences while keeping personal content private from other users. Its Siri requests can use on-device processing or Apple’s Private Cloud Compute, depending on the task.

HomePod mini 2 has no camera or display, giving it a simpler physical privacy profile. It uses microphones for Siri requests and can recognize different household members by voice when supported features are enabled. Likewise, Siri requests use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute.

Both devices support smart home security features, including Sound Recognition for compatible smoke and carbon monoxide alarms.

My take: If you’re uncomfortable having a camera-equipped device in a shared space, HomePod mini 2 may feel like the more straightforward choice.

Apple HomeView vs HomePod mini 2: Price and availability

The price difference is significant enough to influence the decision.

That makes HomeView exactly twice the price of the HomePod mini 2. Wall-mounted HomeView accessories can add to the cost, with Apple’s listed mounting options starting at $59.95 for the USB-C wall connector and $79.95 for the wired AC mount.

Before deciding whether it’s worth the extra cost, explore the Apple HomeView features worth knowing about.

Which one should you buy?

After comparing the two, I’d base the decision on how you want to interact with your smart home rather than which device has the longer feature list.

Buy Apple HomeView if you want a visual smart home hub. It lets you check security cameras, make FaceTime calls, follow recipes, and manage connected devices all in one place. It’s particularly appealing for households where several people can benefit from a shared display. But you’ll pay extra for those visual features.

Buying HomePod mini 2 would be wise if listening to music, Siri, and smart home accessories control are all you need. At $149, it costs half as much as HomeView, making it a more affordable way to add a smart speaker and home hub to your Apple setup.

Ultimately, I’d choose HomeView for its visual features and HomePod mini 2 for its compact design and lower price. Consider which features you’ll use most often before making your decision.

You may also buy both for different rooms. HomeView can sit in a kitchen or family room, while HomePod mini 2 handles music in a bedroom or office. Apple supports multiroom audio across compatible HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay speakers.

Final thoughts

The Apple HomeView vs HomePod mini 2 comparison isn’t about choosing the more powerful device. It’s about deciding how you want technology to fit into your everyday routine.

HomeView has a touchscreen, camera, entertainment, Siri AI, and visual smart home controls. HomePod mini 2 is designed for 360-degree audio, voice commands, and a compact design, with Siri AI support arriving in a future software update.

If I wanted a device to make family routines and smart home controls easier to manage, I’d lean toward HomeView. If I wanted music, voice control, and connected-home features without spending $299, I’d choose HomePod mini 2.

The best choice is the one you’ll use every day. A smart display is worth the extra money only when its screen makes your home more convenient.

title.rendered: Apple HomeView is here, but is this $299 smart home hub worth buying?

content.rendered:
Apple has finally given the smart home a screen of its own. Announced on October 13, 2026, Apple HomeView is a new smart home display powered by Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.

It combines a 7-inch Liquid Retina touchscreen, personalized profiles for up to six people, FaceTime, entertainment, and smart home controls in a device designed for tabletop or wall mounting.

Here’s everything you need to know about the Apple HomeView hub’s specifications, features, privacy protections, price, and limitations before deciding whether it deserves a place in your home.

Apple HomeView specs at a glance

Here’s a quick look at the key Apple HomeView specifications and buying details.

Note: The tabletop and wall-mounted versions have the same starting price, but they aren’t identical out of the box. The tabletop version includes a color-matched USB-C cable and power adapter. On the other hand, the wall-mounted version requires separately purchased mounting and power accessories, which can increase the total cost.

10 Apple HomeView features worth knowing about

1. A 7-inch display designed for any room

The first thing I like is that HomeView doesn’t look like a traditional tablet propped up on a stand. It has an aluminum enclosure, a compact square display, and a domed speaker base that makes it look more like a dedicated piece of home equipment.

The 7-inch Liquid Retina display connects to the base through a stainless steel hinge, allowing you to tilt the screen to find a comfortable viewing angle. It is available in four colors, and the USB-C cable included in the box matches the device’s color.

Apple also offers a separate wall-mounted version in silver and space gray. Rather than taking up counter space, it can sit in an entryway, hallway, or another shared area where household members can check information and control connected devices.

2. New viewing experience in your home

A screen in a shared space needs to be useful without becoming distracting. Apple appears to have considered that with HomeView’s display technology and customizable faces.

The 7-inch display has a resolution of 1088 × 1088 pixels at 220 pixels per inch. It supports True Tone, which adjusts the display’s appearance to suit the surrounding light, and automatic brightness that ranges from 500 nits down to 0.3 nits.

HomeView also adjusts the information displayed on screen based on viewing distance. From across the room, it can display simpler information that’s easy to read at a glance. Move closer, and the interface can present richer details.

3. Customizable Apple HomeView faces

Apple is also borrowing the idea of customizable faces from its other devices, giving the display more personality than a conventional smart home dashboard.

  • Photos face: Displays personal photos with Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while blurring the foreground and background.
  • Shared albums: Turns HomeView into a digital photo frame that family members and friends can contribute to.
  • Flow face: Responds dynamically to physical presence and movement, making the display feel more interactive.
  • Snoopy face: Features animations that change with the time of day, weather, and sporting events.

These faces help HomeView work as both a practical screen and something that looks at home in a living room or bedroom.

The distinction I find interesting is that Apple isn’t treating the display as something that should always show a grid of smart home controls. Sometimes, it can simply show photos or useful information and blend into the room.

4. Siri AI could be HomeView’s biggest advantage

Siri AI could be what makes Apple HomeView more than just another smart display. Apple says its updated assistant offers more natural conversations, broader world knowledge, improved music discovery, and the ability to understand what’s on screen.

Here are the key features worth knowing about:

  • Natural conversations: Ask questions and follow up with additional requests without treating every interaction as a separate command.
  • Improved music discovery: Find music using everyday descriptions instead of remembering exact song titles or artists.
  • Personal context: When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI can use relevant information from apps to provide more personalized responses.
  • Actions across apps: Siri AI can help complete tasks using information from supported apps, reducing the need to switch between them manually.
  • Customizable voice: Adjust Siri’s expressiveness and speaking pace on a compatible paired device.

Apple also says conversations started on HomeView can continue in the Siri app, with conversation history syncing privately through iCloud across supported Apple devices.

My take? Siri AI is HomeView’s most promising feature, but its real value will depend on how reliably it handles everyday requests.

5. Personalized profiles for up to six family members

One of HomeView’s most distinctive features is its ability to recognize up to six people by their faces and provide a personalized experience for each person. It can surface personal content from supported apps such as Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My.

Each enrolled user gets a personalized Home Screen with their own apps and widgets. Personal content can remain separate, while shared albums and music remain accessible to the household and guests.

HomeView uses a front-facing camera for face recognition. But note that your personal information in apps such as Messages and Calendar is shown only when the enrolled user is recognized, and their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked.

6. Smart Home controls from a single screen

HomeView is designed to be the central control point for a compatible smart home. Users can control accessories through the touchscreen or by asking Siri AI.

Supported actions include:

  • Turning compatible lights on or off.
  • Adjusting a compatible thermostat.
  • Locking supported smart locks.
  • Opening or closing compatible blinds.
  • Viewing feeds from supported home cameras.
  • Accessing frequently used accessories through the Home Modular face.

The Home Modular face is intended to provide quick access to favorite smart home accessories, so you don’t have to navigate through multiple screens to reach everyday controls.

HomeView works with Apple’s new Home Collection, which includes smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock developed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. It also supports compatible Apple Home and Matter accessories.

7. Home security and camera monitoring

HomeView’s Home Camera face is designed to make household monitoring easier. Apple says it can display up to nine live camera feeds at once.

The device also supports several security-related features.

  • Intelligent camera notifications to recognize people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles in supported footage.
  • Video descriptions to understand what happened in a HomeKit Secure Video clip.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide alarm detection and sending alerts to an iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.

Still, there are limitations to keep in mind. Intelligent camera recognition and video descriptions depend on supported hardware and services, and some features require iCloud+.

8. FaceTime, Messages, and Intercom

Apple HomeView makes it easier to stay connected with family without reaching for your iPhone.

  • FaceTime: Make video calls using the 12MP Center Stage camera, which keeps you in view as you move around.
  • Messages: Read and send messages using Siri or the on-screen keyboard.
  • Intercom: Send voice announcements to other compatible Apple devices around your home, making it convenient to call everyone for dinner or share quick reminders.

These communication features make HomeView more than a smart home controller. It can also serve as a shared family communication hub, especially in busy households where quick calls and announcements are part of everyday life.

9. Entertainment, Photos, and Audio

Apple HomeView brings entertainment and family memories into one convenient display.

  • Entertainment: Access Apple Music, Podcasts, Apple News, Apple TV, and supported third-party apps.
  • Photos: Display favorite pictures and shared albums, turning HomeView into a digital photo frame.
  • Multiroom audio: Play music across compatible Apple devices for a connected listening experience.
  • Handoff: Continue supported audio or video content on another compatible Apple device.

The tabletop model also includes built-in speakers designed to deliver fuller sound, making HomeView useful for enjoying music, catching up on podcasts, or enjoying entertainment while you go about your day.

10. Kitchen features and everyday convenience

Apple HomeView can be a helpful kitchen companion, keeping everyday tasks organized while you cook or get ready for the day.

  • Cooking assistance: Follow recipe steps, track ingredients, and set timers.
  • Find My: Check the location of shared people and compatible Apple devices, including AirTags.
  • Live Activities: Keep track of useful updates, such as timers and music playback, directly on the display.

These features make HomeView more than a smart home controller, adding practical convenience to your daily routine.

Is Apple HomeView really private and secure?

Privacy is especially important for a device that has a camera, microphones, personal messages, calendars, and access to connected home accessories.

According to Apple, HomeView was designed with privacy and security in mind. For instance, on-device processing through Secure Enclave helps protect camera and microphone data, while Private Cloud Compute supports certain Siri AI requests with privacy safeguards.

Moreover, sensitive personal content doesn’t appear even if HomeView recognizes your face. Your paired iPhone or iPad needs to be present and has been recently unlocked.

These protections sound promising!

Biggest downsides I found in Apple HomeView

Apple HomeView looks promising on paper, but I wouldn’t recommend buying it just because it has a touchscreen and a new AI assistant. Several trade-offs could make it a poor fit for some households.

  • High price: At $299, it’s more expensive than many smart displays.
  • Apple ecosystem dependency: Some Siri AI features require a compatible iPhone or iPad. So, it’s less attractive for a household that mainly uses Android phones.
  • Small display: The 7-inch screen may feel limiting for video and entertainment.
  • Extra mounting costs: Wall-mounted versions require additional accessories.
  • Feature limitations: Some capabilities may depend on subscriptions, regional availability, compatible home accessories, or future software updates.

Overall, HomeView’s value depends on how deeply you’re invested in Apple’s ecosystem and whether its convenience justifies the price.

What makes Apple HomeView different from other smart home hubs?

Apple isn’t entering an empty market. Amazon and Google have spent years building smart displays that combine voice assistants, entertainment, and connected-device controls.

HomeView’s strongest argument is its integration with Apple devices. If your household already uses iPhones, Apple Music, FaceTime, and Apple Home accessories, you can use HomeView to bring all these features together in one place with personal profiles.

The Echo Show 8, meanwhile, offers a larger display and Alexa-based smart home controls. It’s ideal if screen size and value matter more than Apple’s ecosystem. Lastly, Nest Hub is the easiest choice for those who want Google services, a photo frame, and smart home features.

Who should buy Apple HomeView?

I think HomeView makes the most sense for people who will use it throughout the day rather than treat it as an occasional voice assistant.

  • Apple ecosystem households: If most family members use compatible iPhones and Apple services, HomeView’s personalized profiles, FaceTime, Find My, and Siri AI could make the premium worthwhile.
  • People building a connected home: HomeView could provide a convenient central interface for controlling your smart lights, cameras, locks, and thermostats.
  • Families that want a shared household screen: The personalized widgets, shared photo albums, recipes, timers, music, and Intercom are appealing if several people will use the device every day.

Before purchasing the device, I would recommend checking three factors: compatibility of your devices with HomeView, availability of Siri AI functions in your language, and whether you’ll use the personalized features often enough to justify $299.

Final verdict: Is Apple HomeView worth buying?

Apple HomeView is an interesting new direction for Apple’s smart home ambitions. It combines a dedicated display, a speaker system, personalized profiles, Siri AI, and smart home controls in one product.

The most compelling idea is the way HomeView is designed to serve an entire household while still providing individual experiences. Its Home Camera face, FaceTime, Intercom, and kitchen features also give it uses beyond playing music or controlling lights.

However, I don’t think it’s a must-have purchase at $299. It’s quite expensive; the best personalized Siri AI features depend on compatible Apple devices, and the wall-mounted model adds accessory costs.

My recommendation is straightforward:

  • Buy Apple HomeView if your household is already invested in Apple products and you want a dedicated screen for communication, entertainment, and smart home management.
  • Choose a cheaper alternative if you mainly need a voice assistant, basic smart home controls, or a larger screen for entertainment.

What do you think about this new smart home hub from Apple? Let me know in the comments below!

title.rendered: Fortnite Reload: Complete list of Kado Thorne quests and rewards

content.rendered:
Kado Thorne, the main villain from Chapter 4 Season 4 (Aug 2023–Nov 2023), has returned to Fortnite Reload as the inspiration for a series of quests. Each of these offers a unique Kado Thorne-themed reward upon completion, including a pickaxe and a few different emotes.

Given Kado Thorne is among the more strikingly intimidating antagonists in Fortnite history, he fits right into the ongoing event’s horror theme. The quests and rewards based on this character are available for players till October 31, when both the Fortnitemares 2026 event and the Fortnite Override season will end.

If you’re tackling the Kado Thorne quests right now and want to take a look at which requirements must be met for acquiring certain rewards, you can check out the table below.

Kado Thorne quests and rewards in Fortnite Reload

The Kado Thorne reward items are tied to Map Mastery Quests in Fortnite Reload. Unlike other types of quests that can be completed across any Fortnite map, these particular quests require you to complete the action strictly in the given map.

Since maps are consistently rotated in Reload, at any given time, only a quest related to the map that is currently active is doable. For instance, Surf City Mastery Quest must be completed when the Surf City map is in session in that mode.

Below, you can check out the Kado Thorne rewards and the requirements you would have to meet to unlock them.

Wrapping up

Fortnite going deep into its repository to roll out new cosmetics based on a nostalgic figure from its long history is something that should catch the attention of veteran players. Hence, the aforementioned Kado Thorne quests provide a fairly strong incentive for players, especially those who own the original skin from Chapter 4 Season 4, to expand their collection with new relevant items.

On the other hand, whether or not the inclusion of these Kado Thorne cosmetics leads to the Kado Thorne skin also showing up more often in online matches is something only time will tell.

FAQs

Can I get the Kado Thorne skin in Fortnite?

Not really. While a range of Kado Thorne cosmetics are up for grabs for those who complete certain quests, none of those items include the villain’s original skin.

Will Kado Thorne skin return to Fortnite in the future?

Highly unlikely because, since its introduction in Chapter 4 Season 4, this skin has never returned in Fortnite via the Item Shop or any other means. However, a variant of the same, the Elite Kado Thorne skin, did come out as part of a cup reward earlier this month (no longer claimable).

Which maps are in rotation in Fortnite Reload?

The current lineup of maps in the Reload mode consists of Stranger Things (map), Surf City, and Nitemare Island.

title.rendered: How to use Low Power Mode on Apple Watch to extend battery life

content.rendered:
Even though newer Apple Watch models offer better battery efficiency, they may not last through a long trip, a camping weekend, or a day full of workouts. GPS tracking, cellular connectivity, and frequent notifications can all affect how long the battery lasts.

Apple introduced Low Power Mode with watchOS 9 to help users extend their Apple Watch battery life without giving up access to the entire device. It reduces power consumption by limiting certain background activities, sensors, and display features.

In this guide, I’ll explain what Low Power Mode does, which Apple Watch models support it, and how to turn it on in watchOS 27.

What is Low Power Mode on Apple Watch?

Low Power Mode is a built-in battery-saving feature that reduces the power your Apple Watch consumes. It disables or limits selected features so your watch can last longer between charges.

Depending on your Apple Watch model, battery condition, settings, and usage, Low Power Mode can significantly extend battery life. For example, you may get up to 38 hours of battery life for the Apple Watch Series 12 with Low Power Mode enabled. The rugged Apple Watch Ultra 4 offers up to 84 hours of battery life.

I find Low Power Mode particularly useful when I want to preserve battery life during travel or outdoor activities but still need access to the watch’s essential functions.

What features will the Low Power Mode affect?

As I mentioned before, Low Power Mode turns off certain features and reduces background activity. However, it doesn’t disable everything. Some features stop working entirely, while others work less frequently or take longer to respond.

Here’s what changes when you enable Low Power Mode on your Apple Watch.

Features that are turned off:

  • Your Apple Watch stops taking Background blood oxygen measurements, including during sleep.
  • Background heart rate measurements, including during sleep, are turned off.
  • Collection of heart data used for hypertension notifications is disabled.
  • Heart rate notifications for irregular rhythm, high heart rate, and low heart rate are turned off.
  • Always-On Display no longer stays continuously visible.
  • Double Tap and wrist flick gestures are disabled on supported models.
  • Your Apple Watch won’t remind you to start a workout automatically.
  • Time in Daylight tracking is turned off.

Features that are turned off when your iPhone isn’t nearby

Low Power Mode also changes how your Apple Watch handles connectivity when your paired iPhone isn’t nearby.

  • Wi-Fi and cellular connections: These connections are turned off until they’re needed for certain activities.
  • Incoming phone calls and notifications: You won’t receive them in real time while your iPhone isn’t nearby. Your Apple Watch retrieves missed calls and notifications periodically, approximately once an hour.

Features that are affected but not completely turned off

  • Phone calls: Making a phone call may take longer.
  • Background App Refresh: Apps refresh their content less frequently.
  • Complications: Information displayed on your watch face updates less frequently.
  • Live Activities: Updates appear less frequently.
  • Siri: Requests may take longer to process.
  • Animations and scrolling: Some animations and scrolling effects may appear less smooth.

If you rely on health measurements, notifications, or automatic workout reminders, consider these limitations before enabling Low Power Mode for an extended period.

Which Apple Watch models support Low Power Mode?

Low Power Mode is a software feature, so you don’t need the latest Apple Watch to use it. You need a compatible model running watchOS 9 or later.

The following Apple Watch models support Low Power Mode:

  • Apple Watch Series 4 and later
  • Apple Watch SE (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Generation)
  • All Apple Watch Ultra models

Important: Supporting Low Power Mode doesn’t mean every model can install watchOS 27. Older watches may continue to use the feature on an earlier compatible version of watchOS.

How to enable Low Power Mode on your Apple Watch

If your Apple Watch is running watchOS 9 or later, you can enable Low Power Mode from Control Center. The following steps also apply to supported models running watchOS 27.

Method 1: From Control Center

  1. Press the side button to open Control Center.
  2. Tap the battery percentage.
  3. Tap Low Power Mode.
  4. Scroll down and tap Turn On to enable it.
  5. You may also see the option Turn On For…, which lets you select a duration, such as one, two, or three days.

When you enable Low Power Mode without selecting a multi-day duration, it generally turns off automatically once the battery charges to 80 percent. If you select a specific duration, the mode can remain enabled for that duration.

When Low Power Mode is active, you’ll see a yellow indicator. The battery percentage control, charging indicator, and Nightstand Mode display also use yellow to indicate the power-saving state.

Method 2: Via Settings

You can also enable Low Power Mode directly from the Settings app.

  1. Press the Digital Crown to open the app list.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Tap Battery.
  4. Select Low Power Mode.
  5. Tap Turn On, or choose a duration if the option is available.

This method is useful if you’re already adjusting your battery settings and want to enable Low Power Mode without opening Control Center.

Note: Your Apple Watch can prompt you to enable Low Power Mode when the battery level drops to 10 percent or lower. Enable it immediately or dismiss the prompt if you want to continue using your watch normally.

How to automatically enable Low Power Mode during workouts

Workouts can consume significant battery power, particularly when you use GPS tracking or other sensors for extended periods. Apple Watch lets you configure Low Power Mode to activate automatically during workouts on watchOS 27.

Here’s how to enable it:

  1. Open Settings on your Apple Watch.
  2. Scroll down and tap Workout.
  3. Turn on Low Power Mode.
  4. You may also toggle on Fewer GPS and Heart Rate Readings to preserve battery during outdoor walking, running, or hiking workouts.

Your Apple Watch will then use Low Power Mode during workouts, helping extend battery life during longer exercise sessions.

Some workout measurements, including heart rate and pace, can continue to be recorded. However, certain background measurements and notifications may be limited, so check your workout settings if you depend on specific metrics.

How to turn off Low Power Mode on Apple Watch

When you no longer need to conserve battery, you can return to normal operation.

  1. Press the side button to open Control Center.
  2. Tap the battery percentage.
  3. Tap Low Power Mode to turn it off.

You can also open Settings > Battery and disable Low Power Mode there.

Your Apple Watch will resume its normal feature behavior, subject to your usual settings and the capabilities of your model.

Wrapping up

Low Power Mode remains one of the most useful Apple Watch features for anyone who wants to extend battery life without giving up access to the entire device. It can be particularly helpful when traveling, camping, exercising outdoors, or spending a long day away from a charger.

With support across older compatible watches and newer models running watchOS 27, you don’t need to buy a new Apple Watch just to use this feature.

My recommendation is simple: enable Low Power Mode when battery life matters more than having every background measurement and notification available immediately. For everyday use, you can turn it off whenever you want your Apple Watch to operate normally.

  • How to use Heart Rate Zone tracking on Apple Watch

title.rendered: Gemini for Mac now opens Antigravity, and Ultra looks like the target

content.rendered:
Google says Antigravity’s agentic coding interface is now available directly in the Gemini app for Mac. The same day, Google made Gemini 4 Argon available to AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. According to 9to5Google, the change is a pill in the top-right corner. It opens the full Antigravity app, and the same button closes it.

Pro gets the model, and Antigravity may stay with Ultra

Google’s post says AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can use Gemini 4 Argon. For Antigravity, the post doesn’t name a tier. 9to5Google reports that Antigravity requires AI Ultra, so treat that as reported until Google confirms it.

If 9to5Google is right, Pro subscribers get the new model in the Gemini app but not Antigravity.

Antigravity opens a separate app from Gemini

Antigravity was already a standalone app on Mac, Windows, Linux, and Googlebook. 9to5Google says Google has shipped updates every few days since May. The Gemini button opens that same app, and it doesn’t add a version inside the chat window. Antigravity 2.0 came out at I/O in May as a desktop app for managing agents. Now it’s one click away from Gemini.

9to5Google says Google points to Gemini 4 Argon’s coding upgrades as the reason for the change, and that you can build apps and web experiences from the same app. Developers will find that useful. Everyone else gets a second app inside Gemini.

Three names changed in the same update

Google also renamed three things in this update. The table lists the old and new names.

Spark on Mac reached US AI Ultra subscribers in beta in July. Google introduced Spark at I/O as a 24/7 personal agent. Task is a plainer name.

Update the app and check your plan first

9to5Google says the pill needs the latest Gemini app for macOS. The app launched in April, so if the pill doesn’t show, check for an update before deciding it’s missing. On Pro, you get Gemini 4 Argon. If the Ultra requirement holds, Antigravity is the part that needs the higher plan.

excerpt.rendered: Gemini for Mac now opens Antigravity from a pill in the top-right corner. Gemini 4 Argon is available to AI Pro and Ultra, but 9to5Google reports Antigravity needs Ultra.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the Kado Thorne skin in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not really. While a range of Kado Thorne cosmetics are up for grabs for those who complete certain quests, none of those items include the villain's original skin.

mainEntity.name: Will Kado Thorne skin return to Fortnite in the future?

acceptedAnswer.text: Highly unlikely because, since its introduction in Chapter 4 Season 4, this skin has never returned in Fortnite via the Item Shop or any other means. However, a variant of the same, the Elite Kado Thorne skin, did come out as part of a cup reward earlier this month (no longer claimable).

mainEntity.name: Which maps are in rotation in Fortnite Reload?

acceptedAnswer.text: The current lineup of maps in the Reload mode consists of Stranger Things (map), Surf City, and Nitemare Island.

title.rendered: Siri on iOS 27 no longer needs “on Spotify” on newer iPhones

content.rendered:
Spotify users can ask Siri for music on iOS 27 without adding "on Spotify" at the end. TechCrunch reports that Spotify announced the change on October 13. It needs an iPhone 15 Pro or newer with Apple Intelligence turned on.

Siri learns which app you use

Siri learns this on its own. If you keep using Spotify, Siri starts sending your audio requests there. That covers specific tracks, albums, podcasts, and audiobooks, along with broader requests like "play workout music." It also handles Spotify features such as "play my DJ," resuming a podcast, searching your library, and making an AI Prompted Playlist.

Spotify’s reason, as TechCrunch paraphrases it, is that people shouldn’t have to word a request around an app name. Dropping the extra words makes hands-free listening feel more natural. The reporting doesn’t describe a setting for picking a default music app. If Siri plays from a different app, you still have to say "on Spotify."

Apple Music is getting its own Siri AI upgrade in iOS 27, which adds conversational requests about artists and songs. Spotify’s change only affects how you start a request.

The fix stops at iPhone 15 Pro

Apple Intelligence sets the minimum. The oldest iPhones that qualify are the iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max. The standard iPhone 15, iPhone 14, and iPhone 13 don’t get the feature, even on iOS 27. Anyone on those phones still has to say "on Spotify."

Siri AI’s launch covers English and eight countries

Apple’s Siri AI launch list covers English in the US, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the UK. Siri AI isn’t initially available in the EU on iOS or iPadOS.

Spotify’s help text describes the no-suffix version as English-only, and says Siri with Apple Intelligence isn’t available in every country yet. TechCrunch describes the feature as global for eligible users, with the EU excluded. Those accounts don’t match, so Apple’s list is the safer guide.

If you have an iPhone 15 Pro or newer and listen in English, try a request without the phrase. Everyone else still needs it.

title.rendered: Apple’s new Apple TV 4K costs $299 and adds four-speaker surround

content.rendered:
Apple announced the new Apple TV 4K at its "Welcome home" event on October 13. It’s the fourth generation, with an A19 chip. Apple says the CPU is up to 50 percent faster than the last model, and the GPU is up to 2x faster. The box costs $299 in the US, or $49.83 a month for six months through Apple Card Monthly Installments. Pre-orders open today in the US and 29 other countries and regions. It ships November 13.

Siri AI works on the 2022 box too

Apple’s headline says the new box is "supercharged by Siri AI." You don’t need this model to get the feature. Apple’s store page says Siri AI is available on the 2nd-generation Apple TV 4K and later, and that includes the 2022 model. If you already own one, Siri AI is not a reason to buy this box.

Siri AI still depends on your iPhone. The owner of the home needs an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad in the Home app, and personal requests need a paired device.

The feature is in beta and launches in English only, in the US, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the UK. Apple says it won’t initially reach the EU on iOS or iPadOS. Anyone outside those countries will have to wait.

Four speakers are the new hardware

Apple says this is the first Apple TV 4K to support four-speaker surround. The rear pair is HomePod mini 2. A HomePod (2nd generation) can go in front if the front and rear pairs match. The speakers find their positions in the room and set timing and levels on their own.

If you already have HomePods, this is an upgrade you can make without buying much else. If you don’t, the Apple TV alone won’t give you surround sound, and the speakers cost extra on top of the $299.

Home hub features need iCloud+ for the Apple Intelligence parts

The Apple TV also works as a smart home hub. You can control the home from anywhere, set up automations, use guest mode, and process HomeKit Secure Video on the device. Apple Intelligence camera descriptions and notification summaries need an eligible iCloud+ plan. If you’re buying for the home features, check that first.

Find My depends on which Siri Remote you have

The Siri Remote keeps its design and adds Find My support with Precision Finding. Apple ties each feature to a remote generation and, in one case, to an iPhone model:

  • Find My: 2nd-generation Siri Remote or later
  • Locate sound: the 4th-generation remote only
  • Precision Finding: the 4th-generation remote, paired with an iPhone Duo, iPhone Air, or iPhone 17 or later (not the iPhone 17e), on the latest iOS

An older remote gets Find My location but not the sound. The sound is the part that helps when the remote ends up between the couch cushions. Apple sells the remote separately.

The leaks got the chip right and the date wrong

Before the event, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that the Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini would reach stores on October 30. The A19 chip matched. So did the look, since a leaked image showed no external design change. The date didn’t. Apple’s date is November 13.

Siri AI is still in beta, so wait for reviews before you buy for it. If you want the surround setup, you’ll also need HomePods.

acceptedAnswer.text: Not really. While a range of Kado Thorne cosmetics are up for grabs for those who complete certain quests, none of those items include the villain's original skin.

mainEntity.name: Will Kado Thorne skin return to Fortnite in the future?

acceptedAnswer.text: Highly unlikely because, since its introduction in Chapter 4 Season 4, this skin has never returned in Fortnite via the Item Shop or any other means. However, a variant of the same, the Elite Kado Thorne skin, did come out as part of a cup reward earlier this month (no longer claimable).
