title.rendered: I tried Workout Buddy in watchOS 27: Meet your AI fitness coach on the wrist

content.rendered:
Apple introduced Workout Buddy in watchOS 26, giving Apple Watch users an AI-powered fitness companion that provides motivational voice feedback during workouts. With watchOS 27, Apple has made this feature more useful by adding new fitness insights, personalized milestone encouragement, and support for workouts without your iPhone nearby.

If you want a little extra motivation during a run, walk, cycling session, or strength-training workout, Workout Buddy can help you stay focused and understand your progress. In this guide, I’ll explain what’s new in Workout Buddy in watchOS 27, which devices you need, how to set it up, and how to troubleshoot common problems.

What is Workout Buddy on Apple Watch?

Workout Buddy is an Apple Intelligence-powered feature built into the Workout app on Apple Watch. It analyzes your fitness history alongside data from your real-time workout data to deliver personalized audio encouragement.

Instead of simply announcing your distance or elapsed time, Workout Buddy can recognize milestones, highlight your progress, and offer motivation based on your activity history. It can also provide insights into your pace, distance, and workout duration.

Here’s what Workout Buddy can do in watchOS 27:

  • Personalized motivation: Receive encouraging audio feedback based on your fitness history and current workout at the start of your workout.
  • Real-time workout insights: Hear about your progress in areas such as pace, distance, and workout duration.
  • Milestone celebrations: Get encouragement when you achieve milestones, such as completing your fastest 10K, closing your Activity rings, or reaching a yearly distance goal.
  • Post-workout summaries: Hear a recap of your session, including information such as total workout time and calories burned.
  • iPhone-free workouts: Continue using Workout Buddy without carrying your paired iPhone, provided your Apple Watch has a Wi-Fi or cellular connection.
  • Spanish-language support: Use Workout Buddy in Spanish as well as English, subject to device, language, and regional availability.

watchOS 27 has also expanded the fitness data Workout Buddy uses to make its feedback more personal and relevant to your progress. For example, it highlighted that I spent most of my workout in a particular heart rate zone in the last session.

Apple has developed a new text-to-speech engine trained using the voices of real Apple Fitness+ trainers. The result? A voice that sounds more like your upbeat gym coach than a robotic assistant—personalized and energetic.

Requirements to use Workout Buddy on Apple Watch

Before you get started, make sure you meet these conditions:

  • Required Apple Watch: Available on watchOS 26-compatible Apple Watch models (Series 6 or later). However, to enjoy the latest experience, you need an Apple Watch running watchOS 27 or later. It’s available on Apple Watch Series 9 or later.
  • Compatible iPhone: Your Apple Watch must be paired with an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, such as an iPhone 15 Pro or a newer model, running iOS 26 or later.
  • Bluetooth headphones: Connect AirPods or other compatible headphones to your Apple Watch or iPhone to hear audio feedback clearly during workouts.
  • Supported language: Set your device and Siri languages to English or Spanish.
  • Optional: If you want to use Workout Buddy without your paired iPhone nearby, your Apple Watch needs a Wi-Fi or cellular connection.

Apple Intelligence availability varies by device, region, and language. Simply installing watchOS 27 won’t make Workout Buddy available if your paired iPhone or language settings don’t meet the requirements.

How to set up Workout Buddy on Apple Watch

Before you start using Workout Buddy on your Apple Watch, you must first set it up:

  1. Open the Workout app on your Apple Watch.
  2. Turn the Digital Crown to find the workout you want to use. Select a supported one:
    • Outdoor and Indoor Run
    • Outdoor and Indoor Walk
    • Outdoor and Indoor Cycle
    • Hiking
    • Elliptical
    • Stair Stepper
    • High Intensity Interval Training (HIIT)
    • Functional and Traditional Strength Training
  3. Tap the Alerts icon in the top-left corner.
  4. Scroll and tap Workout Buddy.
  5. Toggle on Use Workout Buddy.


  6. Choose your preferred voice.
  7. Tap the Back button to return to the workout screen.

If you want to use Workout Buddy without your iPhone nearby, set it up beforehand and make sure your Apple Watch has a Wi-Fi or cellular connection, you have compatible Bluetooth headphones, and the required Apple Intelligence settings are enabled.

How to use Workout Buddy during a workout

Once everything’s set up, you don’t need to do anything; Workout Buddy activates automatically when you start the workout.

Here’s how it works:

  • In the Workout app, select the workout you enabled Workout Buddy in and hit the Play (Start) button to begin your workout.
  • Workout Buddy kicks in immediately with a motivational phrase like, “Let’s crush that 5K today!”
  • During the session, it provides relevant updates about your progress, including pace, distance, workout duration, and achievements.
  • You may receive audio encouragement when you achieve a notable fitness milestone, such as “Congratulations on crossing 500 miles.”
  • At the end, you’ll get a custom audio recap—“You ran 3.5 miles at an 8:20 pace. Great job beating last week!”

The exact messages vary depending on your workout and recorded fitness data. I received different announcements in every session. Also, don’t expect every milestone to trigger an audio prompt.

The best part is everything is processed on-device, ensuring your privacy while also allowing it to work offline—no internet connection is needed.

Customizing Workout Buddy to match your style

Apple already knew that not all users may be thrilled about the prospect of having an AI cheerleader during a challenging run or other training sessions.

That’s why Apple has made Workout Buddy optional, so you can decide when to use it. You can also choose a voice and mute the feature during a workout if you want some quiet time.

  • You don’t have to use Workout Buddy for every activity. Turn it on for certain workouts and keep it disabled for others.
  • Adjust the voice style: Similar to Siri, Workout Buddy offers multiple voice styles to choose from. To do so, open the Workout app → Select a supported workout → Tap Alerts → Workout Buddy → Choose Voice Style.

  • Mute Workout Buddy: You don’t need to stop your workout if you no longer want to hear the coaching. While your workout is running, swipe right on the workout screen and tap Mute.
  • Customize the on-screen data in your Workout app alongside the voice coaching. To do so, open the Workout app → Select a supported workout → Tap Workout Views → Tap the Edit button and make the desired changes.

Workout Buddy not working on Apple Watch? Try these fixes

If Workout Buddy isn’t responding, providing audio feedback, or appearing in the Workout app, try these troubleshooting steps.

  1. Check device compatibility: Check whether your Apple Watch is running the latest watchOS update. Additionally, the paired iPhone is an iPhone 15 Pro or newer model with iOS 26 or later installed.
  2. Connect Bluetooth headphones: Workout Buddy only works when AirPods or other Bluetooth earbuds are connected to your Apple Watch or iPhone. Press the Side button to open the Control Center → tap the AirPlay icon → ensure your headphones are selected.
  3. Check language settings: Workout Buddy requires your device and Siri languages to be set to English or Spanish.
  4. Enable Workout Buddy for selected activity: The feature isn’t enabled by default. Therefore, ensure that you have enabled it for the supported workout in the Workout app.
  5. Check your watch’s internet connection: If you’re leaving your paired iPhone behind, your Apple Watch needs a Wi-Fi or cellular connection before starting your session.
  6. Check audio volume: Ensure your AirPods or Bluetooth headphones aren’t muted.
  7. Restart both devices: If nothing works, there might be a bug affecting the functionality. Restarting your devices often eliminates such bugs and glitches.

Is Workout Buddy in watchOS 27 worth using?

Workout Buddy is a useful addition for people who appreciate a little encouragement during exercise. The improvements in watchOS 27 make it more practical by adding personalized fitness insights, milestone recognition, Spanish-language support, and the ability to use it without carrying your paired iPhone nearby.

It’s not a replacement for a human coach, and it won’t necessarily provide detailed training advice during every workout. Instead, think of it as an optional fitness companion that makes it easier to stay motivated and track your progress.

If you already use your Apple Watch to track your runs, walks, cycling sessions, or strength workouts, Workout Buddy is worth trying. You can enable it for the activities where you find audio encouragement helpful and mute it whenever you prefer to exercise in silence.

Have you tried Workout Buddy yet? Share your experience or questions in the comments.

title.rendered: Trick or Treat sprites in Fortnite: What they do and how to find them

content.rendered:
Trick or Treat Sprites finally arrived in Fortnite on Thursday, following a lot of anticipation since their in-game announcement some days ago. In doing so, the game has expanded this season’s variant count to six (including base) and raised the total number of unique sprites in Fortnite to a staggering 145.

These Trick Or Treat variants are the latest Halloween-themed addition to Fortnite, as the game celebrates its annual Fortnitemares event through October. Prior to this, on October 1, the devs had shipped a few Halloween-inspired sprites alongside themed changes to the map and gameplay, particularly in the Battle Royale mode.

How to get Trick Or Treat sprites in Fortnite

Similar to how it is with other variants, you have a bunch of different ways you can get your hands on a Trick Or Treat sprite. These include self-sufficient approaches as well as a collaborative effort, giving players ample freedom on how to go ahead with things.

1. By using cheat codes

Perhaps you are most likely to find success sooner if you go down the route of searching cheat codes and using them. These are widespread throughout the Fortnite map and offer you all kinds of sprites, ranging from the Legendary-tier Deer Sprite and the Rare-tier Birthday Sprite.

These cheat codes are in high numbers across POIs, such as Cluster Coast, Green Hill Zone, Heatwave Harbor, Shaken Sanctuary and Sunken Shores. But, if you don’t want to scour a particular location a cheat code, you can also get its location marked by using a Cheat Code Locator. These are up for grabs for free through Fortnite Lobby Hacks and also available for purchase from Extraction Sites.

2. By smashing Pumpkin Chests

Pumpkin Chests are a guaranteed way of obtaining a Halloween-themed sprite from among the Spooky Dash Sprite, Vampire Sprite, Deer Sprite, and the Trick or Treat sprites. It’s worth noting that, unlike other chests, they do not provide anything else like weapons or healing items.

However, Pumpkin Chests are not as commonly found as cheat codes in Fortnite. On top of that, there are only some specific locations, such as Nightmare Neighborhood, Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria, Freaky Fields, and Stone Sanctum, that have more than one or two of them at any time.

3. By opening Rare Chests

Rare Chests used to be a reliable provider of sprites in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 3, but since the rollout of Fortnite Override season, cheat codes have effectively taken their place. What that means is there is a very low chance that these blue chests would help you add a Trick or Treat variant to your sprite collection.

But having a low chance doesn’t mean a zero chance. So, it might still be worth trying your luck whenever you stumble upon these Rare Chests that appear few and far between during a Fortnite match. You can usually find these chests in high concentration in certain areas, including Nightmare Neighborhood, Stone Sanctum, Pac-Man Island, Blinky Island, Cluster Coast, and the maze to the southeast of Stone Sanctum.

4. By taking help from other players

If all that is too time-consuming, you can take the help of another Fortnite player or find someone willing to help in the game’s official Discord server. How this exactly works is that the two players will have to do the indexing of the desired sprite over two matches.

In the first one, you can take a Trick Or Treat sprite from the other player and extract it to index the same into your sprites catalog. In the second match, you can return the sprite to its original owner. To recall the lost sprite, you will simply have to navigate to the Sprites section, in the Override tab, and spend some Sprite Dust, which is another commodity that can be unlocked via the aforementioned Lobby Hacks.

What Trick Or Treat sprite variant does in Fortnite

Trick Or Treat variants are the sole update that has come to the sprites feature in Fortnite this week. It is a special-tier sprite variant and gives those who equip it a chance of receiving candy—an in-game health consumable—when they open a container, like a chest.

In its ability to provide a health consumable, this sprite variant is similar in its purpose to the Birthday Sprite, which provides the Birthday Cake item. Other sprites active in Fortnite Override that boost healing are Onigiri Sprite, Morgana Sprite, and Dumpster Dive Sprite.

Rounding up

Trick Or Treat variants have certainly enhanced the Halloween vibe in the current version of Fortnite. Over the coming days, it will be interesting to see how prevalent and how popular this sprite variant gets in the game’s community. Personally speaking, for now, it appears to be nothing more than an average inclusion in the sprites lineup.

title.rendered: Apple Watch battery draining fast after watchOS 27? Try these fixes

content.rendered:
Have you also noticed your Apple Watch battery draining faster after upgrading to watchOS 27? I’ve been there and can assure you that it’s a temporary issue. Apple says that tasks related to an update can continue running in the background, and some new features can also quietly consume more power than you might realize.

However, if your Apple Watch is still draining unusually fast after a few days, there might be a persistent battery problem. Here are the settings I’d change first.

1. Take advantage of watchOS 27’s automatic battery extensions

Apple has introduced a more proactive approach to battery management. With watchOS 27, the Apple Watch can identify features you don’t frequently use and temporarily pause them to extend battery life.

When this happens, you’ll receive an Extending Battery notification explaining which feature has been paused. You can also turn that feature back on from the notification if you need it.

Apple says the battery-saving system can pause features such as:

  • Gestures
  • Start Workout reminders
  • Raise to Speak for Siri

This means you don’t necessarily need to hunt through multiple settings yourself. You can also enable Low Power Mode if you want your Apple Watch to survive until the end of the day.

Tip: If your battery started draining immediately after installing watchOS 27, don’t start changing any settings. Some tasks related to the update continue running in the background and temporarily affect battery life. I recommend waiting a few days and then checking the battery again. The draining could settle down on its own.

2. Disable AOD (Always-on Display)

Always-On Display is convenient because I can glance at my watch without raising my wrist. But if battery life is my priority, it’s one of the first features I’d sacrifice.

Apple says Always On is available on Apple Watch Series 5 and later, Apple Watch SE 3, and Apple Watch Ultra and later. The display dims when your wrist is down, but disabling Always On completely can improve battery life.

How to disable Always On:

  1. Open the Settings app on your Apple Watch.
  2. Here, locate and tap Display and Brightness. 
  3. Scroll down and tap Always on.  
  4. Toggle off Always On.  

Low Power Mode also disables Always On automatically.

Tip: I wouldn’t disable Always On unless you actually need the extra battery. It’s a convenience feature, not necessarily something you need to turn off on every Apple Watch.

3. Turn off Raise to Wake

If you frequently move your wrist while working, exercising, or simply going about your day, the display can wake up more often than you realize.

Turning off Wake on Wrist Raise prevents the display from activating every time you raise your wrist.  

Here’s how to do it,

  1. Open the Settings app on your Apple Watch.
  2. Here, locate and tap Display and Brightness. 
  3. Now, scroll down and toggle off Wake on Wrist Raise under the Wake section.

I’d consider this an optional battery-saving step rather than a must-do. If you frequently check your watch, the convenience you lose may not be worth the relatively modest battery savings.

4. Limit Background App Refresh

Background App Refresh allows apps to check for updates and new information even when you’re not actively using them. Apple specifically recommends limiting this feature if you’re trying to maximize Apple Watch battery life.

Here’s how to do it,

  1. Open the Watch App on your iPhone and ensure you’re on the My Watch tab.
  2. Here, tap General. 
  3. Select Background App Refresh. 
  4. On the next screen, toggle off Background App Refresh.  

Alternatively, you can leave it enabled and disable it only for individual apps.

There’s one important catch: apps with complications on your current watch face can continue to refresh even when their Background App Refresh setting is disabled.

So if you’re still seeing battery drain, consider simplifying your watch face and removing complications you don’t actually use.

5. Reduce unnecessary notifications

I find notifications to be one of those Apple Watch features that can quickly become excessive.

Every unnecessary notification can activate the display and trigger haptic feedback. If dozens of apps are allowed to alert you throughout the day, the constant interruptions aren’t particularly useful—and they can contribute to unnecessary battery use.

Here’s how to reduce notification permissions,

  1. Open the Watch App on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Notifications.
  3. Review the apps listed there. Disable notifications for apps you don’t need on your wrist.
  4. Also, scroll down and toggle off the apps you do not want notifications from under the Mirror iPhone Alerts From section.

I’d keep notifications for calls, messages, calendar events, and other genuinely important apps while removing everything else.

6. Check battery health before blaming watchOS 27

Sometimes the problem isn’t watchOS at all. The battery itself may simply be getting old.

Apple Watch batteries are consumable components, and their capacity decreases as they chemically age. Apple provides a Maximum Capacity reading so you can see how your battery compares with when it was new.

Here’s how to check Apple Watch battery health:

  1. Open Settings on your Apple Watch.
  2. Tap Battery.
  3. Tap Battery Health.
  4. Check Maximum Capacity.

You can also use the Battery section to view recent battery usage and charging information.

If the watch reports that the battery needs service, changing display settings or disabling notifications isn’t going to fix the underlying problem.

7. Disable Haptic Feedback

As I already mentioned, the Apple Watch is a tool for notifying users. However, you can make do with either sound or haptic feedback, which acts as an indicator when you receive a notification. Here’s how you can disable Haptic feedback on your Apple Watch,

  1. Open the Watch App on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Sound & Haptics.
  3. Tap on Haptics and select the Off option on the next menu.

8. Use a strong Wi-Fi or cellular connection

Connectivity can also affect battery life.

Apple says Wi-Fi and cellular connections use less battery when the signal is strong. If you’re in an area with consistently weak Wi-Fi or cellular coverage, the watch may consume more power while trying to maintain a connection.

If you’re going to spend a long period somewhere with poor coverage, consider using Airplane Mode when you don’t need connectivity.

This is especially worth remembering if you have a cellular Apple Watch.

9. Update watchOS

The watchOS version running on your Apple Watch might be infested with bugs that could lead to battery draining. Apple is renowned for fixing bugs quickly, and if a software bug leads to battery drain, any further updates of watchOS might help. Here’s our step-by-step guide on updating watchOS on your Apple Watch.

Tips to improve your Apple Watch’s battery life 

  • Enable Workout Power Saving mode: If you’re doing a long workout and don’t need every available sensor measurement, you can use the Apple Watch’s workout power-saving options to reduce battery consumption.
  • Disable Environmental Soundtracking: When you enter a zone with loud sounds, the Apple Watch detects unsafe sound levels and notifies you. However, this is one reason for battery drain, and if you want to save battery and live in a rather quiet place, here’s how to disable Environmental Soundtracking.
  • Reduce Animations: If you don’t care much about animations on your Apple Watch, turning on Reduce Motion reduces the animations. Less animation = less power consumption.
  • Avoid Heat While Charging: Avoid charging or leaving the Apple Watch in hot environments, including direct sunlight, for extended periods. Heat can accelerate battery aging and reduce the battery’s long-term capacity.

Signing off

I wouldn’t call every battery drop after watchOS 27 a software bug. Apple itself notes that background tasks can temporarily affect battery life after an update, so the first thing I’d do is give the watch a few days before making major changes.

If the drain continues, I hope these steps help improve your Apple Watch’s battery life. And if you’re using a newer Apple Watch, watchOS 27 now makes some of this easier by automatically suggesting battery-saving changes when it detects that extending battery life would be useful.

If you have any other queries about the battery life of your Apple Watch, leave a comment below, and I’ll do my best to provide a solution.

  • How to turn off Optimized Battery Charging on Apple Watch
  • How to mirror your Apple Watch to Your iPhone
  • How to turn on Live Translation in a conversation on Apple Watch

keyPoints.title: Disable AOD (Always-on Display)
keyPoints.explanation: Turning off the Always-on display on your Apple Watch Series 5 and above can significantly save battery life.

keyPoints.title: Disable Raise to Wake
keyPoints.explanation: Deactivating the Wake on Wrist Raise feature helps conserve power by preventing the watch display from lighting up with wrist movements.

keyPoints.title: Use Dark Watch Faces
keyPoints.explanation: Opt for dark-themed watch faces since OLED screens light up only active pixels, reducing battery consumption.

keyPoints.title: Disable Background App Refresh
keyPoints.explanation: Turning off background app refresh prevents apps from updating in the background, which reduces unnecessary battery drain.

keyPoints.title: Reduce Notification Permissions
keyPoints.explanation: Limiting notifications to only essential apps prevents the display, sound, and haptic alerts from draining your watch's battery.

title.rendered: Unable to update watchOS 27 on Apple Watch? Here’s how to fix it quickly

content.rendered:
Apple’s watchOS 27 brings plenty of new features to the Apple Watch, including smarter Siri, a redesigned app grid, improved Smart Stack interactions, and new health and fitness features. But getting the update installed isn’t always as smooth as expected.

If your Apple Watch is stuck on “Unable to Check for Update,” “Unable to Install Update,” or the update simply refuses to download, don’t worry. I’ve put together the most useful solutions to fix the watchOS 27 update issue and get your watch running the latest software in no time.

1. Check compatibility

Before troubleshooting, confirm that your Apple Watch and iPhone meet the minimum system requirements for watchOS 27.

  • Your Apple Watch must be Series 9 or later, Apple Watch Ultra 2 or newer, or Apple Watch SE 3.
  • You also need an iPhone 11 or later, or iPhone SE (2nd generation or later)
  • Your iPhone must be compatible with iOS 27 and already updated to it.

If your Apple Watch or iPhone doesn’t meet these requirements, the watchOS 27 update won’t appear.

2. Perform the basic checks

Once you’ve confirmed compatibility, ensure these basic conditions are met before updating:

  • Update your iPhone to the latest iOS 27 version for perfect sync.
  • Make sure your Apple Watch has at least 50% battery.
  • Place the Apple Watch on its charger during the update.
  • Connect both your iPhone and Apple Watch to a strong and stable Wi-Fi network. If your internet feels slow, restart your router and disable any VPNs.
  • Ensure Bluetooth is enabled on your iPhone.
  • Keep your iPhone and Apple Watch close to each other.

These simple checks can solve many update problems without requiring you to reset anything.

3. Restart your iPhone and Apple Watch

A restart is one of the first things I’d try if watchOS 27 refuses to install. Temporary software or connection problems can sometimes prevent the update from working correctly.

Since your watch updates through the iPhone’s Watch app, restart both devices.

Restart Apple Watch

  1. Press and hold the Side button until the Power options appear.
  2. Tap the Power button, and you will see the Power Off Slider.
  3. Swipe right on the Power Off Slider to switch off your Apple Watch.
  4. Wait a few seconds, then press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears.

Restart iPhone

  1. Press and hold the Power and one of the Volume buttons simultaneously until the Power Off slider appears.  
  2. Drag the Power Off slider to the right to turn off your iPhone. 
  3. Wait for a few seconds, then press & hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears on the screen.

If a standard restart doesn’t help, try performing a hard reboot on your iPhone.

After both devices restart, open the Watch app and go to General → Software Update to check again.

4. Free up space on your Apple Watch

Insufficient storage is one of the most common reasons why watchOS updates fail. The update file needs adequate space to download and install.

On your Apple Watch, go to Settings → General → Storage and wait a moment for the Watch to calculate how much storage is being used.

If you’re running low on space, remove things you no longer need, such as:

  • Unused apps
  • Downloaded music
  • Podcasts
  • Photos
  • Offline content

Once you’ve cleared up space, restart your Apple Watch and try installing watchOS 27 again.

5. Check Apple’s System Status

Sometimes the problem has nothing to do with your Apple Watch.

If Apple’s update servers are experiencing heavy traffic or an outage, you may see errors when trying to download watchOS 27.

Check Apple’s System Status page and check the “watchOS Software Update” section.

If Apple is experiencing an outage, there’s not much you can do from your end. Wait for the service to return to normal and then try the update again.

6. Unpair and re-pair your Apple Watch

If you’ve tried everything above and the update still won’t install, you can try unpairing and pairing your Apple Watch again.

This creates a fresh connection between your iPhone and Apple Watch and can resolve persistent syncing or communication problems.

Before doing this, make sure your Watch is backed up. Your iPhone should automatically create a backup of your Apple Watch when you unpair it.

Once you’ve unpaired the Watch, pair it with your iPhone again and check for the watchOS 27 update. I would only try this after the simpler fixes have failed.

7. Factory reset Apple Watch

A factory reset should be your last resort, especially if you’re troubleshooting an update problem.

It removes your personal data and settings from the Apple Watch, so make sure you have a backup before proceeding.

To erase the Watch directly:

  1. On your Apple Watch, go to Settings → General.
  2. Scroll down to Transfer or Reset → Pick Erase All Content and Settings.
  3. Enter your passcode to confirm your choice.

After the reset, set up your Apple Watch again and check whether watchOS 27 is available.

If you’re still unable to install the update after a reset, I’d recommend contacting Apple Support rather than repeatedly resetting the Watch.

Wrapping up

And that’s it; these are the most reliable ways to fix the “Unable to Update watchOS 27” issue on your Apple Watch.

We hope these troubleshooting steps help you get back on track and enjoy all the exciting new features Apple packed into watchOS 27. If you’ve found a different method that worked for you, share it in the comments below — it might help someone else too.

title.rendered: How to install watchOS 27 on your Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Apple has released watchOS 27, bringing some of the biggest changes to the Apple Watch in recent years. The update introduces Siri AI, a smarter and more conversational Siri experience, along with a dedicated Siri app that lets you revisit previous conversations and start new ones right from your wrist.

Moreover, the Workout Buddy now works independently of the iPhone, the new dynamic app grid makes it easier to find your most-used apps, and a new single-tap gesture lets you interact with Smart Stack widgets using one hand. watchOS 27 also expanded Cycle Tracking support for perimenopause and menopause.

If you have a compatible Apple Watch, there is plenty to explore in watchOS 27. But before you install it, you should first check whether your Watch and paired iPhone meet Apple’s requirements. Here’s everything you need to know about watchOS 27 compatibility and how to update your Apple Watch.

Is your Apple Watch compatible with watchOS 27?

While Apple typically provides 5 years of software updates for Apple Watch, watchOS 27 no longer supports the Apple Watch Series 8, Series 7, Series 6, first-generation Ultra, or second-generation SE.

Here’s a complete list of Apple Watch models that support watchOS 27:

  • Apple Watch Series 12
  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2
  • Apple Watch SE 3

So, if you have an Apple Watch Series 8 or older, you cannot install watchOS 27. Your Watch will remain on the latest version supported by that model.

What iPhone do you need for watchOS 27?

There is another important requirement that is easy to overlook.

To update to watchOS 27, you need:

  • iPhone 11 or later, or
  • iPhone SE (2nd generation or later)
  • Updated to iOS 27 or later

This means simply owning a compatible Apple Watch isn’t enough. Your paired iPhone must also meet Apple’s requirements.

Requirements to install watchOS 27

Before I start any Apple Watch update, I prefer to get everything ready first. It saves a lot of frustration if the update takes longer than expected.

Here’s what you should check:

  • Update your iPhone to the latest iOS 27 or later.
  • Ensure the battery is at least 50% on both the iPhone and the Apple Watch.
  • Connect your iPhone and Apple Watch to a Wi-Fi network.
  • Keep your Apple Watch within the connection range of your iPhone to prevent disconnection.
  • Place the Apple Watch on its charger before starting the installation.
  • Make sure you have enough free storage on the Apple Watch for the update.

Do you need your iPhone to update watchOS 27?

Not necessarily.

Apple allows compatible Apple Watch models to download and install watchOS updates directly from the Watch itself. However, the Watch still needs to meet Apple’s compatibility requirements, and using the paired iPhone remains the more convenient option for many users.

How to update Apple Watch directly

One of the easiest things about recent watchOS versions is that I don’t always need to reach for my iPhone to start an update.

If your Apple Watch is connected to Wi-Fi, you can update it directly.

Follow these steps:

  1. Open Settings on your Apple Watch.
  2. Scroll down and tap General.
  3. Navigate to Software Update.
  4. Wait while your Apple Watch checks for an available update.
  5. If an update is available, tap Download and Install.
  6. Tap Proceed. Enter your Apple Watch passcode if prompted.
  7. The Apple Watch will restart once the update is installed.

The installation can take some time, so I wouldn’t start the update right before leaving home or heading to work.

How to update Apple Watch with your paired iPhone

For most people, updating through the iPhone is probably the simplest method. Whenever an Apple Watch update is available, your paired iPhone will notify you.

If you intend to update through the iPhone, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Watch app on your iPhone.
  2. Make sure your iPhone and Apple Watch are connected to Wi-Fi.
  3. Tap General and select Software Update.
  4. Wait for the iPhone to check for available watchOS updates.
  5. On the next page, tap Download and Install Now.
  6. Enter your iPhone passcode.
  7. Read the terms and conditions. Once you’ve read the terms and wish to proceed, tap Agree.
  8. You might be asked to enter the Apple Watch passcode; once you do, the update process will begin.
  9. A progress wheel will appear on the Apple Watch. Plug the Apple Watch into a charger to prevent it from dying during the update process.
  10. Once the update is installed, the Apple Watch will restart and run the latest software version.

Note: Once the installation starts, don’t restart, turn off, or disconnect the iPhone or Apple Watch unless Apple specifically instructs you to do so. The Watch may restart several times during the update. That’s normal, so don’t panic if the screen goes dark or the Apple logo appears.

What if watchOS 27 doesn’t appear?

If you don’t see watchOS 27 under Software Update, don’t immediately assume something is wrong.

I would check these things first:

  • Check your Apple Watch model. The supported list starts with Series 9, Ultra 2, and SE 3.
  • Your iPhone must be an iPhone 11 or newer, or an iPhone SE (2nd gen or newer), and it needs to run iOS 27.
  • Update your iPhone to iOS 27 first before trying to install watchOS 27.
  • Put the Apple Watch on its charger even if the battery is already high enough.
  • Give the update some time. Major watchOS updates can take a while to download, prepare, and install. A progress bar that appears stuck for a while doesn’t necessarily mean the update has failed.

All set with watchOS 27

Updating to watchOS 27 is a simple way to bring new features, smarter tools, and useful improvements to your Apple Watch. Once you confirm that your Watch and iPhone are compatible, the installation only takes a few steps.

With features like Workout Buddy, smarter Siri, the redesigned app grid, improved Smart Stack, new health features, and Liquid Glass refinements, there is plenty to explore after the update.

So, is your Apple Watch ready for watchOS 27, or are you still wondering which new feature you should try first?

step.text: You may be asked to enter your Apple Watch passcode. Enter it to start the installation.

itemListElement.text: Enter your Apple Watch passcode on the watch screen.

step.name: Keep the watch charging during the update
step.text: A progress wheel will appear on your Apple Watch while the update installs. Keep the watch on its charger and do not interrupt the process.

itemListElement.text: Leave Apple Watch on the charger until the update completes.

step.name: Wait for the restart
step.text: Once installation finishes, your Apple Watch will restart automatically and run the latest software version.

itemListElement.text: Wait for the watch face to reappear before using the device.

keyPoints.title: Compatibility of Apple Watch with watchOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Most Apple Watch models released from Series 6 onward, including Ultra, Series 11, 10, 9, 8, 7, and SE (2nd and 3rd gen), support the latest watchOS 26 update.

keyPoints.title: Requirements for updating to watchOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: To update, ensure your iPhone runs iOS 16, both devices have at least 50% battery, are connected to Wi-Fi, and are within range of each other.

keyPoints.title: Updating Apple Watch without iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: You can update directly from your Apple Watch by connecting it to Wi-Fi, charging it, and navigating to Settings > General > Software Update to install the latest version.

keyPoints.title: Updating Apple Watch via iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Use the Watch app on your iPhone to download and install updates by connecting both devices to Wi-Fi, then following the on-screen instructions, including entering passcodes if prompted.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Updating to watchOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Updating ensures your Apple Watch has the latest features, fixes bugs, and optimizes performance, allowing you to enjoy new functionalities like Liquid Glass UI, Workout Buddy, and Live Translation.

title.rendered: WhatsApp adds a new Liquid Glass menu to iPhone chats

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is rolling out a new control at the top of iPhone chats that opens a shortcut menu for common conversation settings. The button shows a contact’s photo, name, and online status or last seen, and uses Liquid Glass styling to keep the text readable over different chat wallpapers.

WABetaInfo spotted the feature in WhatsApp for iOS version 26.39.75, which is available on the App Store. It is reaching some users whose accounts already have WhatsApp’s Liquid Glass chat interface, with a broader rollout continuing over the coming weeks.

The new button opens shortcuts inside a chat

Tapping the header button opens a pop-up menu from the top of the conversation. For one-to-one chats, it includes Search, Contact info, Media, links and docs, Chat theme, Disappearing messages, and Mute. Group chats add a shortcut to add members, while business chats get a similar set of options.

The menu gives users a quicker way to reach common chat tools without opening the full contact or group info screen. Search is one of the shortcuts, building on WhatsApp’s new way to search messages on iPhone. The menu acts as a quick-access layer; it does not remove the existing contact and group information pages.

The shortcuts cover both quick lookups and conversation settings. Search can help when you remember part of a message but not where it appeared, while Chat theme and Disappearing messages let you adjust a thread without searching through its info screen. The update does not add new tools to WhatsApp; it shortens the route to options already in the app.

This change is limited to the header inside an open conversation. It does not replace WhatsApp’s bottom tabs or move channels into the Chats tab.

Liquid Glass styling helps with busy wallpapers

The contact name in a transparent chat header can be hard to read when it sits over a busy wallpaper. The new control gives the text a Liquid Glass background that adapts to the image behind it, and the pop-up menu uses the same style.

The update also makes the header do more than identify the person or group. Users can see a contact’s online status or last seen and open common controls from one tap. For groups, the extra add-members option can help admins get to a frequent task faster.

The feature is rolling out gradually, so installing the compatible version does not guarantee the new button will appear immediately. WABetaInfo says some beta testers also have access, but WhatsApp has not announced when it will reach everyone.

WABetaInfo’s rollout notes do not describe a manual setting for the button. If it is missing, users can keep WhatsApp updated and wait for the feature to reach their account.

title.rendered: Mac shipments fell 11.3% in Q3, but Apple gained PC market share

content.rendered:
Apple shipped 5.9 million Macs in the third quarter of 2026, down 11.3% from a year earlier. Its share of the worldwide PC market still rose to 9.5% because the overall market fell much faster, according to IDC’s preliminary tracker.

Worldwide traditional PC shipments dropped 20.1% year over year to 62.7 million units. Apple’s shipments fell from 6.7 million in Q3 2025, but its market share increased from 8.5%. That is a relative gain, not Mac growth: Apple shipped fewer computers than it did a year ago.

Apple’s decline was smaller than most leading PC makers

Apple stayed in fourth place in IDC’s vendor ranking, behind Lenovo, HP, and Dell. Lenovo shipped 14.9 million PCs, HP shipped 10.3 million, and Dell shipped 7.6 million. Their shipments fell 22.6%, 30.9%, and 25%, respectively. ASUS ranked fifth with 5.5 million shipments and an 8.6% decline, the smallest drop among the top five.

IDC’s figures are preliminary estimates of shipments to distributors or end users, not a count of Macs bought directly by consumers. The tracker covers traditional PCs, including desktops, notebooks, and workstations; it excludes tablets and x86 servers. IDC did not publish a Mac-by-model breakdown with this release.

The broader market also weakened from the previous quarter. PC shipments fell 9.1% sequentially, even though Q3 is normally stronger than Q2. The decline follows a 3.8% year-over-year drop in Q2, making this the second consecutive quarter of contraction.

Earlier buying and higher prices weakened Q3 demand

IDC says PC makers and distribution channels bought inventory early in the year to get ahead of memory-driven price increases. That pulled some demand out of Q3 and left sellers working through stock instead of placing the usual seasonal orders. Ongoing supply constraints and higher prices, which IDC links to the AI data center buildout, added to the slowdown.

That pressure reaches Mac buyers too. iGeeksBlog previously covered Apple’s price increases amid higher memory and storage costs. Earlier this summer, some MacBook Air configurations also faced longer delivery estimates, though that report does not establish current availability.

IDC expects retailers and PC makers to offer promotions if inventory stays high, but it does not expect prices to fall back to year-ago levels. A weaker economic outlook could also keep demand under pressure through the rest of 2026 and into 2027.

Market share rose while Mac shipments fell

Apple’s higher share shows it held up better than Lenovo, HP, and Dell during a difficult quarter. It does not mean the Mac business expanded: IDC estimates fewer Macs shipped, and ASUS declined less. The next results will show whether Apple can keep that relative position as the industry clears inventory and manages higher component costs.

title.rendered: Apple announces October 13 “Welcome home” event

content.rendered:
Apple has set Tuesday, October 13, for an event that hints at a home-focused announcement, using the words “Welcome home” in a teaser shared by its marketing chief. The company has not named any products yet, but reports point to a refresh of its smart home lineup.

Apple has confirmed the date, not the lineup

Welcome home. October 13. https://t.co/ChelGSDOTI

— Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) October 8, 2026

Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing, posted the teaser on October 8. 9to5Mac reports that Apple invited press to an in-person “Apple Experience” in Tribeca, New York City, starting at 9 a.m. ET on October 13.

Apple has not published a product list or said whether it will stream a full presentation online. That leaves the event format and any public video unconfirmed; it may be a press experience rather than one of Apple’s usual keynote broadcasts.

The tagline is the clearest clue to the subject. Apple already sells HomePod speakers and Apple TV, but it has not said whether either line will get an update next week. The company has also not announced a new smart display or hub.

A smart home hub is the leading rumor

Bloomberg has reported that Apple is preparing a screen-equipped home hub alongside updated versions of HomePod mini and Apple TV. Those products remain rumors until Apple announces them. iGeeksBlog has previously covered the October product launch plans and the smart home hub’s rumored launch timeline.

One earlier report described a 7-inch display paired with a HomePod-like speaker, with tabletop and wall-mounted versions in development. A hub could give Home controls and Siri a fixed place in a shared room, while a refreshed speaker or TV box would update products customers already use at home. Apple has not confirmed the design or features, and the teaser does not reveal what any device might look like or how it would work.

Recent reports have also mentioned Apple working with LG on home accessories. The reported Apple-LG lineup remains unconfirmed, and Apple has not said whether those products will be part of next week’s experience. The event could bring one product announcement or a wider Home refresh; the invite and teaser do not settle that question.

What to watch for on October 13

The event starts at 9 a.m. ET in New York, or 6 a.m. PT and 6:30 p.m. IST. Apple has not shared pricing, release dates, availability, or any product details. If the company adds a public stream or product pages, those would confirm whether the press experience is tied to a broader launch.

For now, “Welcome home” signals the theme, not a product list. The smart home hub is the biggest rumored change, while updates to HomePod mini and Apple TV would be more familiar refreshes. Apple’s announcement next week will show whether the reports match its plans.

excerpt.rendered: Apple will hold a home-focused event on October 13, but it has not named products or confirmed a livestream. A smart home hub and device refreshes remain rumors.

title.rendered: Freddy Krueger boss in Fortnite: How to find and defeat him

content.rendered:
Freddy Krueger from A Nightmare on Elm Street is a part of Fortnite’s annual Halloween event this year, Fortnitemares 2026. As a result, the iconic villain has not only been introduced in the Shop as a cosmetic item, but he has also been put on the Battle Royale map as a rather challenging boss.

There is a strong incentive for confronting and eliminating Freddy in Fortnite, owing to his signature claws named Freddy’s Nightmare that he drops as mythic loot. Players can use the same for the duration of the match and gain a significant edge in close combat against enemies. Read on to find out where you can find Freddy and how you can take him down to claim this weapon as a reward.

Freddy Krueger location in Fortnite

To come across Freddy Krueger in Fortnite Battle Royale is not particularly difficult, given he is exclusively found wandering in the Nightmare Neighborhood, located to the north-east of Green Hill Zone and to the south of the Pac-Man island. You will usually find him closer to the central part of this POI, walking on the pavement. Additionally, you can take the help of the skull icon that appears on the map once you’re in close proximity to him.

However, it is kind of tricky to be able to know it’s Freddy when you do come across him. That’s because the Nightmare on Elm Street antagonist can shape-shift and sometimes takes the guise of the character known as The Order. In this form, the fight with him can be triggered when you interact, via the chat option, with the character he is portraying.

In other instances, you can encounter Freddy in his own flesh and blood. But keep in mind that, in his true form, he will attack you on sight. So, it’s recommended to anticipate this in advance if you are planning to approach him when he is in his usual look.

How to defeat Freddy Krueger and unlock Freddy’s Nightmare mythic

Going up against Freddy Krueger is just as tricky as identifying him when he is using a disguise. As soon as you start the fight, the disfigured devil will come sprinting to slash your character with his clawed glove.

The part where the face-off gets tricky is when Freddy dodges your attacks by teleporting to different nearby spots. It must also be noted that he can even copy the appearance of the player character in the middle of the fight, leaving the latter briefly confused.

Since the boss’ claw glove deals significant damage with each hit, it’s best to evade him when he is charging and to dodge his attacks. In the small window between those attacks, you can rely on basically any weapon of Uncommon or higher rating to eliminate Freddy sooner rather than later. For ending the face-off as fast as possible, make sure to go for headshots.

Fortnitemares bosses available right now

Excitingly, Freddy Krueger isn’t the only horror IP character that has been absorbed into Fortnite as a boss. Apart from him, Five Nights at Freddy’s characters such as Bonnie the Rabbit, Freddy Fazbear, Chica the Chicken, and Foxy the Pirate Fox are also available as boss fights.

While Bonnie and Chica spawn in random locations, Freddy and Foxy can be found lurking at Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria—the game’s take on Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza, which was the setting for the 2014 survival horror title. Unlike Freddy, the FNAF bosses can be possessed, letting the player use their skin and also get an extra life.

As the Fortnitemares event continues, it will be intriguing to see what else Fortnite devs have under the wraps. Beyond the collab-based cosmetics, more horror-oriented gameplay additions, such as new bosses and match overrides, could freshen things up over time.

title.rendered: 50 Stunning 4K Dynamic Island Wallpapers for iPhone

content.rendered:
These wallpapers work the Dynamic Island into the artwork, whether a character hangs from the pill or a dark background blends it away. The gallery supports iPhone 14 Pro and Pro Max and newer models that include Dynamic Island, including iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

The 50 downloads keep a tall iPhone shape, but their resolutions vary. Each button now shows the file’s pixel size so you can pick the largest version available.

What Is a Dynamic Island Wallpaper?

These backgrounds place a character, object, or graphic around the pill-shaped cutout. iPhone 18 Pro models have a smaller Dynamic Island than earlier Pro models, so some older artwork may sit a little differently. Check the Lock Screen preview and adjust the crop before saving.

The files are portrait images in three sizes: 1109 × 2400, 1170 × 2532, and 1179 × 2556 pixels. iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max displays are 1206 × 2622 and 1320 × 2868 pixels, so iOS enlarges these downloads to fit. Choose the largest version available for the sharpest result. The result? Your iPhone’s screen feels more dynamic, personalized, and visually appealing.

Tips for choosing the perfect Dynamic Island wallpaper

  • Pick the largest file size listed under a design. A close aspect ratio helps prevent cropping, but more pixels keep the image sharper on larger screens.
  • Keep the main artwork clear of the clock and widgets on your Lock Screen.
  • If the artwork points to or wraps around the Dynamic Island, check the preview on your own model before applying it. The cutout is smaller on iPhone 18 Pro models.
  • Dark backgrounds help the pill blend in; bright lines and characters make it stand out.

Note: Each Download button lists the image dimensions. Save the file to Photos before setting it as wallpaper.

Best Dynamic Island Wallpapers by category

1. Cute & Whimsical Dynamic Island Wallpapers

Playful, charming designs featuring adorable characters and lighthearted scenes that bring a smile to your iPhone screen.

Cute Bear

Add a touch of charm and whimsy as a cute bear peeks out from behind the Dynamic Island on your iPhone. Embrace the magic of this wallpaper and add an extra layer of enchantment to your device.

Download

Minions Fun

This Minion-themed Dynamic Island wallpaper will give you a heavy dose of fun every time you unlock your iPhone. Tap the download button to watch these lovable characters bring life to your device with their antics.

Cute Cat

Aesthetic Outdoors

This aesthetic Dynamic Island wallpaper will infuse your iPhone with a touch of elegance and style. Its captivating design will give your device a unique and eye-catching look. If you’re a fan of the outdoors, tap the download button now!

Futuristic Cyberpunk

Step into the future with this electrifying wallpaper with cyberpunk vibes. Whether you’re a fan of retro-futurism or modern digital art, this wallpaper is sure to turn heads and give your iPhone a distinctive, futuristic edge.

5. Nature & Scenery Dynamic Island Wallpapers

Serene landscapes, sunsets, and scenic elements that bring a touch of the outdoors and relaxation to your device.

Summer Sunset

Walking Robot

Where to Find More Dynamic Island Wallpapers: Try These Apps

For more choices, browse these iPhone wallpaper apps. Their catalogs change, so search for “Dynamic Island” or “notch” and preview a design before saving it.

  • Vellum Wallpapers: Curated wallpaper packs and a daily image.
  • Walli: Wallpapers from independent artists.
  • Zedge: A large wallpaper library with search.
  • Backdrops: Original designs in categories such as minimal, abstract, and pop culture.
  • Unsplash: A photo library rather than a dedicated wallpaper catalog.

Tip: Search for “Dynamic Island” within these apps, or browse categories like “notch,” “pill,” or “cutout” for the best fit!

How to Set a Dynamic Island Wallpaper on Your iPhone

Setting up your new wallpaper is quick and easy:

  1. Download a wallpaper and save the image to Photos.
  2. Open Settings and tap Wallpaper.
  3. Tap Add New Wallpaper, then choose Photos and select the image.
  4. Adjust the crop in the preview so the artwork lines up with Dynamic Island.
  5. Tap Add, then choose Set as Wallpaper Pair or Customize Home Screen.

Use the preview to line up characters and graphics with the cutout before saving.

Tip: Some wallpapers are designed specifically for the Lock Screen, while others shine on the Home Screen. Experiment to find what works best for you!

Final thoughts

The Dynamic Island is more than just a notch—it’s an opportunity to express your style and creativity. With the right wallpaper, you can make your iPhone truly stand out. Try a few different looks, play with colors and themes, and enjoy the endless possibilities!

title.rendered: How to use Visual Intelligence on iPhone to translate, search, and ask ChatGPT

content.rendered:
Apple first introduced Visual Intelligence with iOS 18.2, a feature that could recognize what your iPhone’s camera saw in real time. With iOS 27, Apple takes it a step further. Visual Intelligence is now closely integrated with Siri AI, giving the iPhone a much better understanding of what is in front of the camera and what is displayed on the screen.

Here’s a full guide on how to use Visual Intelligence on your iPhone.

What is Visual Intelligence?

Visual Intelligence is an Apple Intelligence-powered feature that combines on-device AI with real-time visual understanding. It debuted with the iPhone 16 series and requires at least an A17 Pro chip with an advanced Neural Engine for fast, private processing.

With it, your iPhone can recognize and extract details from what your camera or screen shows—from identifying a plant to translating a menu, finding products online, or getting instant help from ChatGPT and Siri AI.

In iOS 27, Visual Intelligence is more closely connected to Siri. It can:

  • Identify objects and places
  • Ask questions about something in front of the camera
  • Search the web for visually similar images
  • Recognize plants and animals
  • Read, summarize, and translate text
  • Get information about businesses
  • Analyze food and provide nutritional information
  • Interact with restaurant bills
  • Extract information from documents and cards
  • Turn information from flyers into calendar events
  • Take actions based on what the camera sees

Apple also lets Visual Intelligence work with screenshots, so you don’t need to physically point your camera at something if the information is already on your iPhone.

Which iPhones support Visual Intelligence?

Visual Intelligence requires an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone.

Apple says Apple Intelligence on iOS 27 is available on:

  • iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16e, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max
  • iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max
  • iPhone Duo

Apple Intelligence availability can vary depending on the device, language, and region.

If you are unsure whether your iPhone supports the feature:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Apple Intelligence & Siri or Siri.
  3. Check whether Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone.

How to access Visual Intelligence on iPhone

iOS 27 gives several ways to launch Visual Intelligence.

Method 1: Use Siri Mode in Camera

If you have Siri AI enabled, this is the most direct way to use Visual Intelligence.

  1. Open the Camera app.
  2. Swipe through the camera modes until you reach Siri.
  3. Point your iPhone camera at whatever you want to understand.
  4. Tap the Siri button to learn about what is in the frame.

For example, I can point the camera at an unfamiliar object and tap the Siri button to get information about it. Then swipe down on the response and continue the conversation with follow-up questions.

Method 2: Use Camera Control

If your iPhone has the Camera Control button, press and hold it to let Visual Intelligence analyze the scene, then choose one of the suggested actions or ask a question.

First, you need to set it up:

  1. Open Settings on your iPhone.
  2. Select Camera and tap Camera Control.
  3. Scroll down and toggle on Press and Hold under the Launch Visual Intelligence section.

This remains one of the quickest ways to access Visual Intelligence on supported iPhones.

Method 3: Use the Action Button

If your iPhone doesn’t have Camera Control, you can assign Visual Intelligence to the Action button on supported models.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Action Button.
  3. Swipe through the available options.
  4. Select Visual Intelligence.
  5. Press and hold the Action button whenever you want to use it.

Method 4: Add Visual Intelligence to the Lock Screen

You can also customize your Lock Screen to add Visual Intelligence as a control.

  1. Unlock your iPhone with Face ID and touch and hold your Lock Screen.
  2. Tap Customize.
  3. Tap the minus button on the control you want to replace.
  4. Then tap the plus sign and select Visual Intelligence from the available controls.
  5. Tap Done.

This is particularly useful when I want to analyze something quickly without navigating through multiple menus.

Method 5: Add Visual Intelligence to Control Center

You can also launch it from Control Center.

  1. Swipe down from the top-right corner of your iPhone.
  2. Look for the Visual Intelligence control.
  3. Tap it to launch the feature.

If you don’t see it, tap the + button to customize Control Center and add the Visual Intelligence control.

How to use Visual Intelligence on iPhone

The real appeal of Visual Intelligence isn’t simply recognizing objects. What makes iOS 27 interesting is that the feature can turn what the camera sees into an action.

Here are some of the most useful things you can do.

1. Ask Siri about anything in front of your camera

This is one of the biggest changes in iOS 27.

Instead of simply identifying an object, I can ask a question about it. For example, I can point my camera at a cricket ball and ask: “How do you play cricket?”

Siri AI can identify the object and continue the conversation with a follow-up answer.

To try it:

  1. Open Camera.
  2. Switch to Siri mode.
  3. Point the camera at an object.
  4. Tap the Ask button on the left.
  5. Type or dictate your question.
  6. Wait for Siri’s response.

You can continue asking questions without starting over. Also, all these conversations are available in the Siri app for future reference.

This makes Visual Intelligence feel much more like an interactive assistant rather than a simple visual search tool.

2. Identify plants and animals

Visual Intelligence can recognize plants and animals through the camera.

To use it:

  1. Open Camera.
  2. Enter Siri mode or launch Visual Intelligence using your preferred shortcut.
  3. Point your camera at the plant or animal.
  4. Tap the suggested identification or tap the Siri button to know what you’re looking at.
  5. Follow the results for additional information.

If the system isn’t confident about an identification, treat the result as a suggestion rather than a guaranteed answer.

3. Identify places and businesses

Visual Intelligence can also help when you’re walking around a new area.

Point the camera at a business or location, and Visual Intelligence can provide relevant information about it, depending on what’s available in your region.

For supported businesses, you may see details such as:

  • Business information
  • Opening hours
  • Website
  • Contact information
  • Menu or ordering options
  • Other relevant actions

4. Get nutritional information from food

This is one of the more interesting iOS 27 additions.

Point your iPhone camera at food or a meal, and Visual Intelligence can provide information about it, including nutritional information and ingredients when the system can determine them.

To try it:

  1. Open Camera.
  2. Switch to Siri mode.
  3. Point the camera at your meal or food.
  4. Look for a suggested action or tap Ask.
  5. Ask something such as, “What is this food?” or “What can you tell me about this meal?”

The results are meant to provide useful information, not replace professional dietary or medical advice.

5. Split a restaurant bill

Visual Intelligence can now do more than read a restaurant receipt. With the updated Wallet app in iOS 27, Siri can offer a Split Bill option when you point your camera at a receipt.

To use it:

  1. Open Camera.
  2. Switch to Siri mode.
  3. Point your camera at the restaurant check.
  4. Wait for the suggested action.
  5. Tap Split Bill with Apple Cash if it appears.
  6. Follow the on-screen instructions to divide the bill.

The exact payment options depend on region and service availability.

6. Search for similar products and images

Visual Intelligence can perform a visual search when you want to find similar items online, similar to Google Lens.

For example, if I see a pair of shoes, bag, piece of furniture, or gadget I like, I can point my camera at it and search for visually similar results. You can also directly buy the product from the search results.

  1. Open Visual Intelligence.
  2. Point your camera at the object.
  3. Tap the Search button on the right.
  4. Review the visually similar results.
  5. You can also draw a circle to highlight the product you want to search.

This is particularly useful when I don’t know the name of the product I’m looking at.

7. Translate text with Visual Intelligence

Visual Intelligence can understand text through the camera and provide actions such as translation.

To translate text:

  1. Launch Visual Intelligence.
  2. Point your camera at the text.
  3. Let your iPhone analyze it or tap the Siri button.
  4. Choose the Translate option when it appears and tap Continue.
  5. Then tap on any text to listen to the translation or copy it. You can also change the translation language from here.

I often use this feature for signs, menus, labels, notices, and other printed text when traveling. No need to open the Translate app separately!

Visual Intelligence can also provide options for summarizing or reading text aloud when appropriate.

8. Summarize text you see

You don’t always need to read a long notice or document yourself.

Point your camera at the text, and Visual Intelligence can offer a Summarize and Read Aloud action.

This can be useful for:

  • Notices
  • Documents
  • Posters
  • Instructions
  • Long printed messages
  • Information sheets

The available actions depend on what Visual Intelligence detects.

9. Turn a flyer into a calendar event

Visual Intelligence can recognize event information from posters and flyers and help you add it to Calendar. This is much faster than manually typing the event name, date, time, and location.

To use it:

  1. Point your iPhone camera at the flyer or poster.
  2. Launch Visual Intelligence.
  3. Wait for the event information to be recognized.
  4. Tap the Add to Calendar option to create the event.
  5. Review the pre-filled details, such as the event title, dates, and location. You may also add invitees, reminder alerts, and other relevant details.
  6. Once satisfied, tap the checkmark to add it to your calendar.

Similarly, the feature also helps me add contacts from visiting cards.

Also read: I tried the Calendar app in iOS 27. These new features actually save time

Visual Intelligence also works with your iPhone screen

This is where Visual Intelligence becomes particularly useful.

You don’t have to point your camera at everything. If something is already displayed on your iPhone, you can use screenshot-based Visual Intelligence to understand it.

For example, I can use it on a product page, social media post, website, document, photo, message, screenshot of an app, and much more. Apple provides a dedicated Visual Intelligence experience for content on the iPhone screen.

Use Visual Intelligence on a Screenshot

  1. Open the content you want to analyze.
  2. Quickly press and release the Side button + Volume Up buttons together.
  3. Your iPhone takes a screenshot and opens the preview with Visual Intelligence tools.
  4. Depending on what’s on the screen, choose Ask, Search, or another suggested action. Siri AI can use on-screen awareness to answer questions and take actions based on screen content.
  5. Highlight a specific object if you only want to analyze part of the screenshot.

The tools shown at the bottom can change depending on the content in your screenshot.

The best feature is the ability to highlight an object on the screen. Suppose I’m looking at a screenshot containing several products, but I only want information about one of them. In such a case, simply take a screenshot and highlight the specific object.

Visual Intelligence can then search for that specific item rather than treating the entire screenshot as a single image. This is especially useful when comparing products or researching something I see on social media.

How Visual Intelligence works with ChatGPT

If you’ve used Visual Intelligence in earlier iOS versions, you may remember seeing an Ask option that handed questions to ChatGPT.

That integration hasn’t disappeared from Apple’s broader Apple Intelligence experience, but the iOS 27 Visual Intelligence workflow is more tightly connected to Siri AI.

If you still want to use ChatGPT for some queries, here’s how:

  1. Open Siri mode in Camera or take a screenshot of the content.
  2. Tap the Ask button and then enter this query: “Ask ChatGPT to tell me what this is”
  3. For the first time, it will prompt you to enable ChatGPT. Tap Turn On on the prompt.
  4. Then follow the one-screen instructions to enable the extension.
  5. Now, again enter your query added with “Ask ChatGPT,” and ChatGPT will continue the conversation.

The Siri app saves such conversations as well.

Change Visual Intelligence settings in iOS 27

Apple has added settings that let you control how Visual Intelligence behaves.

To find them:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Siri.
  3. Depending on your device and configuration, you can find settings such as:
    • Highlight to Search: Enable it to let Siri AI automatically search the web when you highlight something while using Siri mode in Camera or screenshots.
    • Automatic Visual Look Up: This allows your iPhone to automatically identify objects and places that appear in screenshots.

These options are useful if you want Visual Intelligence to be more proactive.

Visual Intelligence vs Visual Look Up: What’s the difference?

These two features can sound confusing because both can identify things.

Visual Look Up is Apple’s traditional image-recognition feature. It can recognize certain objects, animals, plants, landmarks, laundry symbols, car dashboard signs, and other visual content.

Visual Intelligence is broader. It combines Apple’s visual understanding with Apple Intelligence to let you search, ask questions, summarize information, translate text, and take actions based on what your camera or screen shows.

In iOS 27, Visual Intelligence also works closely with Siri AI, making it more conversational.

Things to keep in mind

Visual Intelligence is powerful, but I wouldn’t treat every result as authoritative. AI-generated information can sometimes be incomplete or incorrect, especially when the camera can’t clearly see the subject.

I also need to remember that feature availability varies by:

  • iPhone model
  • Region
  • Language
  • Apple Intelligence availability
  • Siri AI availability
  • Third-party service availability

Apple specifically notes that Apple Intelligence features aren’t available in every language or region, and Siri AI is currently offered as a beta feature on iOS 27.

For anything involving health, nutrition, finances, or other important decisions, I would verify the result using a reliable source rather than relying on Visual Intelligence alone.

Final thoughts

Visual Intelligence has come a long way since Apple introduced it.

In earlier versions of iOS, I mostly thought of it as a smart camera feature that could recognize objects, translate text, identify plants, or search for products. iOS 26 expanded the idea by letting Visual Intelligence understand what was on my screen.

With iOS 27, Apple takes the next step by bringing Visual Intelligence deeper into Siri and the Camera app. I can now ask Siri what I’m looking at, follow up with another question, search for similar images, or take an action based on what my iPhone sees.

If Apple continues improving Siri AI and Visual Intelligence in future updates, I think this could become one of the most useful parts of Apple Intelligence. What do you think about this feature? Let me know in the comments below!

title.rendered: I tried Live Translation with AirPods on iOS 27: here’s how it actually works

content.rendered:
The first time I tried Apple’s Live Translation with AirPods in iOS 26, the idea felt almost too futuristic: someone speaks another language, and I hear what they’re saying in my own language through my earbuds.

With iOS 27 and the latest Apple Intelligence features, Apple has continued expanding this feature, making it available on more AirPods models and supporting more languages. If the other person doesn’t have compatible AirPods, you can still use your iPhone to show or play the translated version of your response.

Here’s everything you need to know about Live Translation on AirPods, including the compatible iPhones and AirPods, supported languages, setup process, and how to use it during a real conversation.

What is Live Translation on AirPods and how does it work?

Live Translation is an Apple Intelligence feature that lets compatible AirPods translate what another person is saying into your preferred language in real time.

The experience is designed to be hands-free. Instead of repeatedly typing or looking at your iPhone, you can listen to the conversation through your AirPods while the Translate app provides a transcript on your iPhone.

Here’s how it works:

  1. The other person speaks in their language.
  2. Your AirPods and iPhone capture the conversation.
  3. Your iPhone processes the translation.
  4. You hear the translated speech through your AirPods.
  5. The Live tab in the Translate app can show a transcript of what was said.
  6. You can respond in your language.
  7. Your iPhone can show the translated response to the other person or play it aloud through its speaker.

This makes conversations smoother, whether you’re traveling, on a call, or speaking with someone in person.

Prerequisites

Before you can use Live Translation on your AirPods, make sure you meet these requirements:

  • AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, or AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation, AirPods 5 (both models), AirPods Max 2 updated to the latest firmware.
  • iPhone 15 Pro or later running iOS 26 or newer.
  • The Apple Translate app installed on your iPhone.
  • Apple Intelligence enabled on your iPhone.
  • Supported languages downloaded to your iPhone

Apple notes that availability can vary by language and region.

Supported languages

Currently in iOS 27, Live Translation supports these languages:

  • English (US and UK)
  • French
  • German
  • Italian
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese (Brazil)
  • Spanish (Spain)
  • Chinese (Mandarin, Simplified)
  • Chinese (Mandarin, Traditional)

Apple may add more language support in upcoming updates.

How to download languages for Live Translation

For Live Translation to work, you’ll need to download language models in advance. For example, if someone is speaking Spanish and you want to hear English, download both Spanish and English.

  1. Put on your AirPods and connect them to your iPhone.
  2. Now, open Settings → [Your Name] AirPods near the top of the screen.
  3. Here, locate and tap Live Translation (Beta).
  4. Next, select the languages you want to download.

Once downloaded, the entire translation process happens on-device to keep all conversation data private.

How to set up Live Translation on AirPods

Unlike Adaptive Audio, Live Translation isn’t enabled by default. Here’s how to set it up:

  1. Wear your AirPods and connect them to your iPhone.
  2. Now, open the Translate app and tap Live at the bottom.
  3. Under Their Language, select the language the other person is speaking.
  4. Under Your Language, select the language you want to hear through your AirPods.

This gives you full control over the conversation settings, including the languages and whether translations are spoken aloud or displayed on-screen.

You’re now ready to start the translation.

How to start Live Translation on AirPods

Once setup is complete, Apple gives you several ways to activate Live Translation, so you don’t have to open the Translate app every time.

Method 1: Use the Translate app

  1. Open the Translate app.
  2. Tap Live.
  3. Choose the languages.
  4. Tap Start Translation.

This is probably the easiest method when you first use the feature.

Method 2: Use your AirPods

If you have AirPods 4 with ANC, AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 2, or AirPods Pro 3, press and hold the stems on both AirPods at the same time.

If you’re using AirPods Max 2, press and hold the listening mode button.

Method 3: Ask Siri

You can also say: “Siri, start Live Translation.”

Siri will start the feature when the necessary settings and supported hardware are in place.

Method 4: Use the Action Button

If your compatible iPhone has an Action button, you can configure it to launch Translate.

When you’re wearing your AirPods, using the Action button can automatically start Live Translation.

Method 5: Use Control Center

You can also add Translate to Control Center and use it as a quick way to access Live Translation.

  1. Swipe down from the top-right corner of your iPhone.
  2. Tap Translate.
  3. Start Live Translation.

How to use Live Translation during a conversation

Once Live Translation is running, you don’t have to keep looking at your iPhone.

Simply listen while the other person speaks. Your AirPods will automatically detect the other person’s language, reduce background noise with ANC, and deliver translations directly to your ears.

When it’s your turn to respond:

  1. Speak normally in your language.
  2. Open the Live tab in Translate if you need to show the other person what you’re saying.
  3. Tap the Play button to have your iPhone speak the translated response through its speaker.

If the other person also has compatible AirPods and has started Live Translation, they can hear your translated response through their AirPods. Otherwise, use your iPhone to communicate your response.

Tip: When I’m using Live Translation in a noisy place, I use the iPhone’s microphones to improve the translation input. You may move your iPhone closer to the other person so their speech is captured clearly in addition to the microphones on your AirPods.

Live Translation in Calls

Live Translation isn’t limited to face-to-face conversations.

Apple also supports Live Translation during calls in the Phone app and FaceTime while you’re wearing compatible AirPods.

On an active call:

  1. Start or answer the call normally.
  2. Tap More.
  3. Tap Live Translation.
  4. Choose the language.
  5. Tap Start Translation.

The other person is notified that the call is being translated. As you speak, they hear the translated version, and their response is translated for you. You can also see an on-screen transcription.

Note: Apple warns that Live Translation uses generative models and that translations can sometimes be inaccurate, unexpected, or offensive. For anything important, you should verify the translation rather than treating it as perfect.

How to stop Live Translation

When you’re finished:

  1. Open the Translate app.
  2. Go to the Live tab.
  3. Tap the X button to stop Live Translation.

Tips for the best experience

To get the most accurate translations, keep these in mind:

  • Keep your AirPods and iPhone updated to the latest firmware and iOS version.
  • Use Live Translation in quiet environments for better accuracy.
  • Keep your iPhone nearby, as it handles the translation processing.
  • Speak naturally but clearly. Very fast speech, heavy background noise, or unclear pronunciation can make translation harder.
  • Download language packs before traveling abroad.
  • Ensure your AirPods are fully charged to avoid interruptions.

Breaking language barriers with AirPods

Apple’s Live Translation for AirPods makes global conversations more natural and effortless. Whether you’re traveling, working, or just connecting with someone in a new language, this feature helps you stay focused on the conversation rather than the translation.

Have you tried Live Translation on your AirPods yet? Share your experience in the comments below.
